strings.YGR_a_codified_division_of_power_desc: The problem of our system is sometimes its extreme murkiness when it comes to the responsibilities and privileges of different classes of bandit. Can a pakhan determine his own economic policy for the region? Do grunts deserve protections? Can a civvie be considered a civvie if he replaces a grunt? All of this must be clarified, all privileges must be settled, so that there are no surprises at the wrong time.
strings.YGR_opportunities_for_profit_desc: The West is rife with left-overs of industry left behind by Bukharin and the subsequent pretenders that sprung up from his state's bloated corpse... and who are we not to use it? The pakhans will be ordered to re-mobilise and repair their local industries as they see fit and ensure that they come to good use. The economy will roar again!
strings.YGR_the_law_of_the_thieves_desc: Well, we aren't animals after all. For all the carrots in the world, there must be a stick, and the laws of the reformed Thieves will be dictated to all the West's gangs, whether they like it or not. If we want to continue, we must all march at least in the same direction.
strings.YGR_the_saviours_of_russia_desc: With the economic systems ironed out, we can safely say the West now produces for us, with our leadership. We have truly secured an important part of our Russian heartland... Now we just must make sure that the people don't forget it! Better pay and such is all good, but the people mustn't forget how much effort we expend on them!“
strings.YGR_moderating_our_image_desc: The last pretenders have created a mirage of us, as if we are some feudal lords or criminals... Which, of course, is completely false! It is time we make people understand we are here for their sake, first and foremost: Russia cannot stand without its pakhans, especially without its Great Pakhan!
strings.YGR_corruption_not_coercion_desc: Those who cannot be bought have died clutching their machine guns and grenades when we smashed through towards the West. Those that are left, on the other hand, CAN be bought. And if they can be bought, and we have all this capital lying around... why not skip the unpleasant violent bits and simply reach a good deal?
strings.YGR_rewarding_the_people_of_russia_desc: With all the praise that reaches the pakhans, we should not forget the average civvie. We are all the people of Russia, unless they rebel against us that is. All ***RUSSIANS*** will be rewarded, good pay, or lands, or whatever they were missing without us.
strings.YGR_russia_in_good_hands_desc: The average socialist will howl that we're dirty capitalists. The average nationalist will rant that we're holding back the greatness of our country. The average monarchist will whine how we're not incest-ridden enough to appoint rulers. The commonality between them? Not a single one will argue that it's worse under us, than it was beforehand.
strings.YGR_stealing_heaven_and_earth_desc: The people are with us, to Hell and back, the West has been lulled into our rule. Now it is time we turn back to more important matters. The East, the frosty resource-rich semi-wasteland is an uncut diamond, we just have to get our hands on it to make it shine, whether its owners like it or not.
strings.YGR_an_offer_they_cant_refuse_desc: In any sort of dealings, one should have leverage, and the greatest leverage is fear. There are many things that a person may fear: guns, knives, bombs. But what do nations fear? Well, looking at modern politics, it seems that nuclear weapons. And don't we deserve a say in international politics? We certainly do.
strings.YGR_a_pay_rise_for_our_geniuses: A Pay Rise to our Geniuses
strings.YGR_a_pay_rise_for_our_geniuses_desc: Considering Russia is a little out of its depth right now, we do not have much of a backbone in nuclear physics. Those nuclear physicists that we DO have are either hiding out in ruined universities or too focused on getting the few crumbs of bread they can find to last a week. Neither of these situations is acceptable, time we treat our geniuses right... for some services, of course.
strings.YGR_stealing_blueprints_from_japan_desc: Japan may not be the ones who developed the A-bomb, but they're certainly one of the best users of it, Pearl Harbour tells the tale. And good results means that they must have some good knowledge on construction, so why don't we get a few frustrated researchers a few million bucks for a quick trip to the photocopier?
strings.YGR_steal_blueprints:
We will use our connection to acquire blueprints from our enemies. 
Increases theoretical development progress by 15%, and monthly progress gain by 3%
strings.YGR_the_russian_uranium_mining_consortiu: Probably the most labour-intensive part of making a bomb is also the one we have the least problems with. Russia's big, and so are its resources, so getting uranium will pass without a hitch. Get a few regional pakhans to cooperate, and we'll have ourselves production numbers to rival the rest of the superpowers!
strings.YGR_and_a_bribe_for_theirs_desc: Nonetheless, there's not enough geniuses to cover the calculations of the average eggheads in R&D. Two vertebrae aren't a backbone, and a couple geniuses aren't a development team, so how about we import some foreign labour? The State cut your program's funding due to demilitarisation? No worries, dear egghead, we have JUST the place for you to be!
strings.YGR_braving_the_black_sun_desc: But while making a bomb is possible, it takes just that one bit too long. Don't have it, can't buy it? Steal it, of course! Then again, if we steal from the US, that is a diplomatic crisis, if we steal from Japan, that is a war, and if we steal from the Reich, that's an existential threat... But wait, what will the BLACK STATE, do about it? Like taking candy from a... well, probably not.
strings.YGR_braving_black_sun_tt: We will prepare the most elaborate plan for the riskiest robbery of all time
strings.YGR_the_greatest_heist_in_history_desc: We measured them up, we scouted the place, it's time we grab the 'hot potato'. Nobody will cry about them missing one... Well, except for them.
strings.YGR_greatest_heist_tt: Ladies and Gentlemen, may the show begin!
strings.YGR_russias_new_chief_desc: At last, Russia's journey to strength and power has truly begun. Under the wise and enriching leadership of our new Great Pakhan, Aslan Usoyan, we at last have the German dogs to our west in sight, and new lands and territories to be put under the administration of the Transitional Government. So long as we keep our trust in Papa Hasan, things can only get better from here.
strings.YGR_destroy_our_enemies_desc: Unfortunately, not all our new citizens think so highly of their new leadership. Thankfully, our reconstruction programs and a few well-placed bribes have gotten many previously dissenting figures steady employment, bread, and a roof over their head, things that many Russians lacked not long ago. For those that still cling to ridiculous ideas like communism, fascism, or liberalism and seek to reimplement their dead ideals by terrorism and force of arms, however, we shall fight fire with fire. No rebel will escape alive.
strings.YGR_reinforce_the_chain_of_command_desc: Reintegrating the former soldiers and officers of the previous West Russian government has not been an easy task. Those personnel deemed too ideologically fanatical must be purged from our ranks before they can harm continued profitable operations, but sometimes we must lose a little money to gain back a big reward. We will assign all the manpower and money necessary to ensure a smooth transition of former West Russian soldiers into our own ranks, and prepare for the ultimate reunification of Russia, all under the absolute leadership of our Great Pakhan.
strings.YGR_from_bandits_desc: Though our origins began as mere criminals and bandits, we have become something greater. We are now leaders of a great deal of territory, and we must strive for something higher than just being gangsters and fighting over streets for extra money. No, we must evolve into something more...unified and civilized.
strings.YGR_to_businessmen_desc: What is crime but a business banned by the law? Whether it's selling drugs, murder-for-hire, or \“protecting\” the small businesses that are the backbone of our economy, we were all just in it for the money. Now that we're the law, we no longer have to worry about pesky things like criminal codes. After all, we're all just trying to make ends meet, aren't we?
strings.YGR_from_gang_to_corporation_desc: Now that total unification seems in sight, it's time we drop any façade about our real intentions. In order to ensure the security, stability, and continuing profitability of the Russian state, all economic assets will be appropriated and reorganized under the control of the All Russian Transnational Company. All will be \“fairly\” compensated for their compliance, for a safe, and secure, Russia!
strings.YGR_our_new_ventures_desc: With a greatly expanded pool of manpower and resources, it is time we begin expanding the offers of our Company to bigger and better things. It's a common tenet of business that one must innovate or die. Given we have very little interest in dying, the only matter that remains is just what lines of work our new Russia will find itself in.
strings.YGR_centralized_admininstration_desc: The old way of things under Jaba Ioseliani was a truly disastrous and degenerate system. Individual pakhans lorded over their little pieces of Russia like feudal lords, treating the people under them like serfs! We may be ruthless capitalists, but we are not reactionaries! From now on, Russia's governance shall be strictly managed from the top, with a bureaucracy based on merit and loyalty to our regime. Corruption and laziness will no longer be tolerated!
strings.YGR_enforcers_on_every_street_desc: It might seem ironic, given that we are ex-prisoners, but it seems we must provide Russia with new police to fix the abject lack of law and order she has suffered from for the last two decades. Petty crimes and felonies alike are at an all time high, from pickpocketing to outright murder and rape. This isn't the way of the Thieves, at least not anymore. We will create a security subsidiary of the ARTNC, to ensure that on every street, our laws are obeyed, our workers are safe, and anyone with...unprofitable ideas are quickly dealt with before they can spread dangerous ideas like \“democracy\” or, Heaven forbid, \“workers' unions\”.
strings.YGR_tax_everything_that_moves_desc: When government and business are one, taxes form an important part of the revenue for our company. Given the sole objective of a corporation is to make profit for its shareholders, it only makes sense that we should bring in as much profit as we absolutely can, especially since running a country is no cheap task! If we can tax it, it will be taxed as much as we can. If you can't pay it? Well, you can always work off your taxes for us. Your salaries will be \“kept for safekeeping\” until your owed taxes are paid in full to the Company.
strings.YGR_set_up_the_facade_desc: However much it jacks up our operating costs, running a country does come with certain responsibilities. People need protection from harm, a roof under their head, a job to work at, schools for their children, and pensions for the old and sick. We are no charity, but if welfare and justice keep our workers productive and healthy, then surely these investments will bring a fruitful return!
strings.YGR_supplying_the_kurds_desc: Though we are the All *Russian* Company, our Great Pakhan is not actually an ethnic Russian. Though he hails from Georgia, Aslan Usoyan is of Kurdish descent, and still has a soft spot for the plight of his oppressed people in the Kurdish homeland. With Iraq and the Middle East in flames, we now have the perfect chance to begin running high-quality weapons and ethnic Kurdish volunteers to fight for the freedom of Kurdistan, and perhaps even gain a potentially very, very profitable stake in this oil and blood rich region of the world.
strings.YGR_the_worlds_miners_desc: If there's one thing Russia doesn't lack, it's natural resources. Millions of our subjects are already employed in mining every kind of metal and mineral there is, and yet so much of it lies in stockpiles! We already have more than enough for our own production, so naturally, it would be best to start selling, and we're not picky. American corporations? Japanese Zaibatsus? French merchants? We don't care! If you can pay the price tag, we'll sell you all the fine metals you can handle.
strings.YGR_anything_for_the_right_price_desc:
If we must be honest, we are still criminals at our root. After all, isn't a criminal just a businessman without enough money to stay out of jail? Though we are more than happy to sell the world cheap goods, cheap alcohol, and good quality metals and weapons, if your tastes are, say, less legal, we won't judge. 

Drugs? We'll get you higher than a kite? 

Prostitutes? Well, do they say Russian women are the most beautiful in the world?

Need you to kill someone? We'll get our hands bloody if you can afford to pay our hitmen. 

We can't promise we'll get you a price your wallet can appreciate for these sorts of things, but chances are, if you're seeking these kinds of services, you're probably rich enough for us to have no right to question your financial decisions. Just get in line, and one of our agents will see you shortly.
strings.YGR_profit_in_the_wind_desc:
Ahh, can you smell it? Profit is one sweet, sweet smell, and it's stronger than ever now. Who the hell would have thought that just a little over a decade ago, we were slaving away in some frozen hellhole in Vorkuta? Now, we are the undisputed masters of Russia. We have made her a force to be reckoned with, and a business to rival the largest corporations on Earth. All of Russia is in our grasp, and we're no longer just hearing profit in the wind.

 	WE'RE HEARING A STORM
strings.YGR_all_hail_the_custodian_desc:
Well, we did it. We have stabilized our government and prepared our future plans, now our greatest challenge until now lays east: we must start mobilising our forces in the Siberian border and prepare for the incoming struggle. Despite the ardous task, with the support of all corporations and capitalists around the world... 

WE WILL PREVAIL!
strings.YGR_reviewing_the_code_desc: The Vory Code is currently under revision, most of our political concerns are redirected to closing this matter as soon as possible.
strings.YGR_redrawn_gang_territories_desc: The redrawn territories gave us the support of the more greedy Pakhans, now our situation is more stable than ever.
strings.YGR_the_renewed_lace_desc: To gain the trust of the people we have decided to reform the lace, with new regulations and clauses now it can be compared to a more classical taxation system.
strings.YGR_formalized_circle_desc: The formalization of the circle grants us the possibility of a better diplomatic game, at the cost of its secrecy.
strings.YGR_secret_circle_desc: Keeping the Circle as a shadow entity of our state gives us the advantage of anonymity while keeping most of our actions secret.
strings.YGR_the_new_vory_code_desc: The Vory code has been rewritten, now it can be used as a basis for running a state with no drawbacks.
strings.YGR_disorganized_admininstration: The status of the admininstration has always been a problem for the bandits, as it is almost unfunctional: coupled with a non-existent bureaucracy, management of the territory is impossible.
strings.YGR_reforming_the_admininstration: With our newly conquered territories, Ioseliani decided that it was time to reform the territorial admininstration, it's a hard task but it must be done if we wish to subjugate our enemies.
strings.YGR_winter_bandits_desc: Our bandits now are equipped to witstand the harsh climate of Siberia: we'll be feared in the snows.
strings.YGR_zlatoust_businessmen_desc: We have spared various businessmen from Zlatoust, now indebted to us, they will do everything we order.
strings.YGR_the_victory_of_the_bandits_desc: We are victorious! We have successfully subjugated every enemy in the region, morale is higher than ever!
strings.YGR_conscript_everyone_desc: Our situation is very dire, we must expand our army at any cost.
strings.YGR_disrupted_supplies_desc: This warlord's supplies have been disrupted by enemy sappers, and its army is facing logistical problems.
strings.YGR_infiltrate_enemy_army_desc: The Low Command of this warlord's army has been infiltrated by their enemies, making the relaying of orders unreliable.
strings.YGR_production_sabotaged_desc: The factories of this warlord were damaged by enemy sappers. They now struggle to reinforce the front.
strings.YGR_Smuggling_category_desc:
Yugra's economic situation is a mess. The bandits are able to survive only with Usoyan's smuggling network, a web that covers the entirety of Occidental Russia. With this handy connections, we will be able to survive, and in the future, fund other Russian warlords in their struggle for reunification... 

But we all know the longer their wars are, the more weared down they will be when we pounce on them.
strings.YGR_send_volunteers_to_kokshatai_tt: We will be able to send two volunteer divisions to {kok_getnamewithflag} to help them in their wars!
strings.YGR_KOK_send_volunteers_to_russians_tt: We will be able to send two volunteer divisions to {ygr_getnamewithflag} to help them in their wars!
strings.YGR_raise_ioseliani_influence_low_tt: Raises Ioseliani's influence by a low amount
strings.YGR_raise_ioseliani_influence_mid_tt: Raises Ioseliani's influence by a moderate amount
strings.YGR_lower_ioseliani_influence_low_tt: Lowers Ioseliani's influence by a low amount
strings.YGR_lower_ioseliani_influence_mid_tt: Lowers Ioseliani's influence by a moderate amount
strings.YGR_raise_usoyan_influence_low_tt: Raises Usoyan's influence by a low amount
strings.YGR_raise_usoyan_influence_mid_tt: Raises Usoyan's influence by a moderate amount
strings.YGR_lower_usoyan_influence_low_tt: Lowers Usoyan's influence by a low amount
strings.YGR_lower_usoyan_influence_mid_tt: Lowers Usoyan's influence by a moderate amount
strings.YGR_prepare_the_troops_tt:
The more £command_power Command Power we have the more £smuta_supplies Military Supplies Weekly Gain we shall receive, the more £army_experience Army Experience we posses the more £political_power_texticon Political Power we will receive. If Yugra finds itself at war, the gifts shall be larger.
  - Military Supplies Weekly Gain: [?Y|+=%1].
  - Political Power: [?pp|+=0].
strings.YGR_hasans_magic_tt: Thanks to Usoyan's contacts, we will begin the construction of new barracks and infastructure in our strategic regions!“
strings.YGR_sabotage_tt: We will unlock new sabotaging decisions!
strings.YGR_weapon_smuggling_tt: We will unlock new decisions to smuggle our weapons!

strings.YGR_THENEWORDER_DESC:
For the better part of three decades, the Vorkuta gulag complex starved, tortured, and killed tens of thousands of Russia's petty criminals. For the better part of nineteen, Jaba Ioseliani and the various gangsters, killers, thieves, dissidents, and ethnic minorities imprisoned within Vorkuta's walls survived their “punishment”, concocting every form of resistance they could. It started with toilet wine (which they later discovered themselves to have invented), then poisonings, then fake guns, before Jaba Ioseliani, a Georgian student-turned-bank robber, pickpocketed a real handgun out of a particularly fat and lazy guard's holster. 

With the means of revolt coming together, a disorganized band of roughly 6,000 hardened convicts, desperate to escape enslavement, launched their first escape attempt. Just as Ioseliani's bank robbery ended poorly, the attempt was a massive failure. However, it was certainly not the last attempt; three dozen were launched between 1957 and 1960. All of these slowly culled the weakest prisoners until they were left with only the toughest, meanest, and smartest among them. Ioseliani's gang, the Vorkutan version of the famous “vory v zakone”, or thieves-in-law, finally took action on the night of January 1, 1960. The starved, languished, yet brutally determined thieves in law that had survived three years of reprisals and worsened conditions took up makeshift clubs and fake guns, storming the armoury. Armed with Mikhail Kalashnikov's latest triumph, the gang killed as many guards as they could as they fled the hellish prison-fortress of the Vorkuta gulag. 

Thousands of men fled alongside the thieves-in-law; members of rival gangs, reactionaries seizing the opportunity, and many other desperate victims of Vasily Blokhin. Thousands of men, all willing to fight to the death in the name of their newfound freedom. The thieves-in-law quickly weaponized these scattered dregs as they went on the warpath, conquering nearly all of the Vorkutan land south of the Reka Usa. Once Blokhin's regime was too destabilized to launch a reprisal, Jaba Ioseliani, now ruler of the Yugra region, founded the Thief Territory; a state ruled entirely by organized crime. The vory v zakone of Yugra, a patchwork group of mobsters, gangs, and petty criminals, rule in their strip of land in the Russian far north. 

Now, Jaba Ioseliani and his band of merry men are faced with a not-so-merry reality; they have a country to run. With everything from food to resources to infrastructure becoming looming problems, the time has come to overcome complacency and take the reins of a state that needs a firm and effective, if a bit inebriated, hand.  

If they aren't successful, that firm hand may be replaced by a whip, in the grasp of the Vorkutlag.
strings.YGR_initial.0.desc:
“...well, what are you, Sharik, tearing your throat? It's like we're crooks here! You were a puppy, I brought you to the house...” sang a loud congregation of drunks, as Jaba wobbled past their little bar. Yugorsk's nights were cold, but tonight was exceptionally freezing; most were drinking with their friends to stay warm, it seemed. Jaba Ioseliani, the de facto head of their new frozen state, was himself piss-drunk, walking home from a particularly raucous drinking session at a bar his friends liked. As he walked past the bar and reached the bombed-out remains of an intersection, Jaba started to think. 

The vodka made it a bit fuzzy, but standing at the curb elicited a sort of mental movement he'd never felt with this much alcohol in his system. Out of nowhere, his mind was surprisingly clear, methodically going through each and every thought; how the wind felt, how his head kind of hurt, why he was drinking when he was head of a whole-ass country. 

A sudden burst of lucidity hit him square in the nostril. 

An entire nation of people. People a lot like him; slightly drunk bandits, but people under his supervision. Their little nation-state, new and happy and drunk as it was, needed a leader. It needed food, water, infra-...infrastructure, that was the word, infrastructure, water, guns, leadership. It needed him, Jaba Ioseliani, to stop his fucking drinking and get off of his ass! 

With a new motivation, Jaba started walking again. It wasn't easy; although his thinking was “clear”, his body was still drunker than an Englishman when their Football Club wins, or loses, or draws, but a bit of swagger, legwork, the assistance of the wall, and heart finally got him to his dwelling. At the moment, he was living in an old pre-Soviet hotel, currently christened as the “Papa Pakhan Palace”, against his wishes. When he entered, he was quickly grabbed by one of Aslan Usoyan's secretaries; several of his underlings were living here, too, until they could find suitable housing. 

“Thank you, Leonid... but I'm... fine, I.. swear...,” Jaba eloquently and articulately slurred. 

“No, sir, I don't think you are,” Leonid, rudely interrupted from a new Mario Fusco book he had found earlier, begrudgingly carried the sole ruler of Yugra up the stairs and into his bedroom. Ioseliani, still in a stupor physically, half-wrestled himself out of an already reluctant hold, waved off his underlings's underling, and sat down at his desk. 

As he shifted from stupor to hangover, Jaba wrote down all of the things he wanted; not a long list, and all of the things everyone else wanted; a much longer list. His men wanted more vodka, the few people outside the thief's life more food. Everyone wanted guns, trucks, oil, money, and more women. 

Jaba went to the ice box, and threw the vodka in it out the window.
strings.YGR_initial.1.desc:
Aram Boghosyan took another long sip of his drink, cards in hand.  Good vodka was sure hard to come by nowadays, wasn't it? He glanced back down to his cards.  16.  Would he take the risk?  Aram was never much of a card-counter, or all that bright in general.  Perhaps if he had done better in school, he wouldn't have spent six years in a gulag.  He gulped down the last of his beer and looked right in the dealer's eyes.

Hit me.

The dealer begrudgingly handed him the 5 of hearts.  Aram's gamble paid off.  For him, Blackjack wasn't all unlike his life in the Mafia.  Every move was a risk, and sometimes it seemed like the best move was to not play at all.  But for every chance he had to go over, for every time the house seemed to rig it against him, Aram survived.  In the frigid north, it was not just brains or brawn that separated the men from the corpses.  It was cunning, and those that were cunning would find themselves rewarded handsomely.

  Holding the wad of cash in his hand, Aram went back to the bar and grabbed a stool, hoping to celebrate once again beating the house at their own game with another shot of their best vodka.  That was, at least, until something caught his eye.  Two somethings, actually, some of the nicest he had ever seen.  “Hey there beautiful, why don't I buy you a drink?” 

 Saturday night was about to get very fun.
strings.YGR_initial.2.desc:
Ioseliani leaned back in his chair, feet up on the desk, reading the report on the recent in-fight with a casino debtor and creditor, his mind filling with a combination of annoyance, yet at the same time, morbid entertainment. 

A knock on the door would pull the pakhan out of his thoughts, “Come in!” Ioseliani barked, sitting forward and tossing the file to the side. 

Rafael Baghdasaryan slipped through the door, his eyes darting around in a nervous manner. “Jaba, we have a problem.” 

“Ah, Raf! My dear, so-called, spy-master! Some news? Usoyan is playing those little games of his? Maybe-” 

“Jaba,” Rafael would interrupt, “It's not ONLY Usoyan, it's worse.” 

“Come on Raf, what could be wo-” 

“Damn it, Jaba! Get your shit together for once! The rest of the pakhan circle's licking their lips for your position.” Rafael's jaw would clench. “There's been rumours going around, rumours that you're losing your grip, that you haven't got the-” 

“Raf, stop being such a damn nervous rash and get your FUCKING point across!” Ioseliani growled, picking between his teeth, his voice dripping with simmering rage. 

“They think you're weak, Jaba. Their forces are on the brink of turning on us. And you know how to prove strength...” Rafael left a meaningful pause. 

Jaba also paused... and then, with an exasperated sigh, pulled himself out of the chair.  

“Damn it all, and I was hoping to have more time... Convene the Circle, it seems I can't manage it peacefully now. After all-”
strings.YGR_initial.2.a: “Better stand and die, than live and crawl.”
strings.YGR_initial.3.desc:
Aslan Ûsoyan sat at his beautiful, pristine, stolen desk, and thought. Since the breakout a few years back, he had mostly sat and thought. He thought about his past; his childhood, or what little of that he had, his time on the streets, and his time in the gulag. He thought about his present; his gang had carved out a hunk of Yugran wasteland, looted what they could, and were now trying to... grow something. If they could get their hands on some good potatoes, they could have some real, fresh food. Could you make naan with potatoes? Finally, he thought about what was to come for their frozen shithole. 

It had been ages since any kind of meeting had been held. The little circle of thieves-in-law they made after the escape had convened once. One time. No one had any idea what the plan was, what to do, what to prepare for. However, Aslan knew there was an opportunity in their stagnation. He could take control. All he needed was a little more time, and he could be the pakhan of the pakhans. 

Suddenly, there was a knock at the door. 

“Boss!” It was Leonid, his secretary. “Come in.” Leonid entered the room, strode to his boss's desk, and excitedly handed him a letter. “It's from Ioseliani. Good news, I can only hope.” He stepped back and waited patiently for Aslan to read the letter. Ûsoyan opened the letter, and began to read the... very short announcement. 

“Aslan Ûsoyan, you have been summoned to attend the next pakhan meeting. You will receive correspondence announcing the date and time promptly.

With kind regards, 

Jaba.” 

Aslan started to sweat. His fingers shook slightly. Now? That slimy motherfucker Jaba chose now to convene a meeting? To fuck with his plans right now? With this meeting, he finally broke the months-long silence, which'll get the other pakhans on his side for a little while longer. A little while too long. 

“So, boss, I take it that's not very good news,” his secretary quipped. “Leonid. Leave the room for a moment.” Leonid stepped out of the office. The grizzled pakhan was left a fuming mess by the news. It was HIM who was supposed to take control of this clown show, not that accursed Georgian. 

His hand had been forced; he needed to change his strategy. From here, there would be a couple options; he could try and convince the others that this meeting was just a ploy to keep them loyal for a little while, again; he could find another pakhan with his same ambitions and form a coalition; or, he could just kill the bastard at the meeting, and take control then and there. 

Once again, Aslan sat and thought
strings.YGR_initial.4.desc:
“Mario drove to the door. BANG! BANG! Revolver fire echoed through the dim hallway, narrowly avoiding him. It would take more than that to kill Mario Fusco, he thought. His assailant aimed his .38 at him, and-” 

CLANG. 

Someone had dropped a tray in the barracks; a sound Leonid had yet to get used to. Back in Vorkuta, things falling to the ground loudly meant someone near you was in trouble, and trouble meant vicious beatings. The guards there were merciless. They'd see you make the smallest mistake and they'd hit you on the spot, not too bad, but never manageable. If you really fucked up, though, they would wait. Sometimes, they would wait hours, sometimes days. All it took was a moment of reprieve; smoking a cigarette, stretching, even squatting down, and they'd pounce. No one ever came back from a Vorkuta beating the same; some went mad after just a couple. Leonid tried to get back to his book, but he kept on thinking, and thinking, about before. 

Vorkuta was a hellhole. Before the “Great Patriotic War”, or whatever they called the desolation of the Russians, it was squalid and unforgiving. Beatings were constant, disease was rampant, and it was much too cold, even for Siberia. Things only got worse after the war. The camp got cleaned up, but they killed all the nice people, everyone still got sick, and it was even colder. Blokhin, the eternal bastard, decided making the guards even meaner was how he would maintain order. 

Like everything else he did, it blew up in his face. 

When Blokhin took control of everything, his first move was to try and wrangle the gangs. He got most of them under his foot, but then he tried to make the Georgian comply. Blokhin failed to see that Jaba was a bigger bastard than even him, and the Vorys had had enough of his Cheka bullshit. Half the prisoners were given guns and cigarettes, if they agreed to shoot at the guards. Not one refused. Political prisoners, gangsters, killers, landowners, even a few old nobles, took those guns and shot at the guards that had beat us for 30 years. Of course, they were much better armed than we were, but we were just well-armed enough to get the hell out of there and set up here. 

Things are a lot better than Vorkuta now. We have money, guns, food, and freedom. Even the army's free. And best of all, we have books now. It'd been 15 years since Leo had read a book, and now he could read whatever he wanted. With a sliver of contentment in his heart, Leonid got back to his book. “His assailant aimed a .38 at him, and fired. The bullet zipped past Mario's round body, hitting the forklift he was driving and crippling the engine. 'Curses! Nobody fucks with the Fusco!' Mario drew his piece and put a bullet in the large man who was chasing him. The blood dyed his black skin red, and as the body fell, Mario sighed and looked down at his pistol. ”You're gonna have to try harder than that to stop the Fusco. After all...'
strings.YGR_initial.5.desc:
Jaba stood out in front of the bustling circle of mob bosses, staring at each and every grizzled criminal veteran as they gossiped and schemed with each other. Their meeting had been a very mixed bag of success; although his security as leader was by no means assured, the position on Vorkuta was clear; as the mad German Goebbels said in the 30s, they wanted total war. As was assumed to be formal, Jaba had prepared a speech to close the meeting. He gave a sharp a-hem, silencing the busy group, and began; 

“Everyone! Bosses, seconds, ground troops, all of you gathered here today! We have gathered, we have spoken, and we have decided. For too long, Blokhin and his hellish gulags have existed on this earth, brutally beating, starving, and killing not only men like us, but innocent men! Men whose only wrongdoing was not being the same as a dead government! Not long ago, it was us in those camps, but we escaped, and those men still in there stayed behind. Now, though, we have an opportunity to save thousands, put thousands more in deserved body bags, and put ourselves on the map.” 

“We have guns. We have men. We have men who can use those guns, and we have men who can aim those guns at Blokhin. So, as thief-in-law of thief-in-laws, I make this demand; we mobilize. We prepare for the inevitable war, the true war, the war that we are meant to fight, the war we have to fight. The people of Yugra; its vory v zakone, soldiers, and common folk, must unite to take down our greatest and deepest opponent. We will depose the king in his barbed-wire casket and bury him in it. When we're done with Vorkuta, there will be nothing left but dust, blood, and the bones of those damn guards, their guns shoved so far up their asses you can only see the butt end.The time has come for war, and we will face Blokhin and his devils.” 

“However, although we have the spirit to rip them apart, we don't have enough machine guns to do it with. If we want to truly and decisively destroy everything Blokhin holds dear, we need more guns. We need better training, we need better equipment. The Saranpaul airport is still being renovated, and we don't have many planes. Not only that, but we know that the gulags have more of all the things we need than we do. If we want to win, we have to be organized. Once we have the organization, we will have the means to reach victory. Once Vorkuta is under our control, we have the means to become a real country. A real country! If we don't gear up and seize this opportunity, it might never come around again. This is it! This is our fight!” 

The room, rather surprisingly for a disunited group of criminal leaders, erupted in unanimous applause. For the moment, the divisions in allegiance disappeared in favor of a united front against their enemy. 

In all aspects, it was a very successful meeting for Jaba Ioseliani.
strings.YGR_initial.6.desc:
“You're late.” 

The foreman looked sternly at the three men. Mikhail Iosifovich Gurevich, Sergey Vladimirovich Ilyushin, and Artem Ivanovich Mikoyan, former plane designers, before their lackluster planes got them thrown into Vorkuta, had been selected to rebuild Saranpaul Airport. On their first day of work, they arrived twenty-three minutes late. Sergey stepped forward, and bowed in apology, “...My deepest apologies, sir. We were held up by a few holes in the road. You understand,” Sergey huffed, “No, actually, I don't. I came up the same way, and I didn't have any trouble with the roads,” said the foreman. Sergey's lie had immediately fallen apart, to the astonishment of approximately no one. “Whatever.” The foreman pulled out a crumpled piece of paper, unfurled it, and read aloud. 

“Mikhail Iosifovich Gurevich, Sergey Vladimirovich Ilyushin, and Artem Ivanovich Mikoyan, you have been hired by the Thieves-in-Law of Yugra to restore and renovate Saranpaul Airport, for the purposes of civilian use and the needs of the thieves-in-law. Gurevitch, you are in charge of designing a new airfield and runway. Ilyushin, you are in charge of redesigning the hangars for larger planes and maintenance crews. Mikoyan, you are in charge of the construction of a new airport facility, designed for all uses that the people of the Thieves' Territory of Yugra would require from it. Are there any questions?” The foreman lowered the paper, and looked out at the three remarkably short men. Artem raised his hand. 

“Thank you, sir, but aren't you, the foreman, supposed to be in charge of this operation?” Artem asked. The foreman sighed. “No, you three are in charge of the operation. I tell my men what you want done, and I have them do it. Are we clear?” “I... think so.” Artem muttered. Ilyushin clicked his tongue, and Gurevich looked out at the battered airfield. “Now, what is our first course of action?” Of the three, Gurevich spoke first. “Repair the airstrip. Once that's done, we'll be able to fly in supplies and diplomats. There's not much out here, but that will suffice while we keep building.” 

The foreman cracked a very, very small smile. “On it, boss.”
strings.YGR_initial.8.desc:
Jaba Ioseliani took a moment to clean his binoculars on his wool coat before putting them back up to his eyes.  Below him, dozens of soldiers were hard at work, digging networks of hidden trenches and building up outposts.  Anti-tank ditches were hidden in leaves and snow, and the whole process was being greatly accelerated thanks to top-notch radios bought from the factories of the Zlatoust Republic.  Jaba laughed under his breath.  After all, the border with Zlatoust was in view from where he was standing.  Soon, he thought, there wouldn't be a border left. 

While the Great Pakhan laughed, the work had already begun within the borders of the Gunsmiths' Republic.  In the barracks, in the officers' mess, and in the factories, the corruption that had always been prevalent in the Republic became the Thieves' greatest weapon.  First taking on the uniform of the Security Forces, before taking on the role of “legitimate businessmen,” the loyalty of several key officials within Zlatoust had been bought with briefcases filled with gold.  Those who did not comply were...convinced through more physical means.  Upon completion of the operation, it would only take one signal to light the spark aflame, and start the greatest heist in the history of Russia.
strings.YGR_initial.9.desc:
A loud knock on the door woke Yevgeny Dragunov from his first nap in a while. “Come in!” He yelled, lighting up a cigarette. The door opened and his secretary entered his office. The spry old woman handed him a sleek, jet-black envelope, adorned with a white star and cat. 

“A letter addressed to you, sir.” The secretary put the letter down on the table in front of Dragunov. He took it and started reading. 

“Prime Minister Yevgeny Dragunov, 

We would like to inform you that your services are no longer needed, and our deal from before is hereby void. We have found a better provider for arms and other equipment, much cheaper than yours. We are cutting all funds and payments. 

Signed, Jaba Ioseliani, the Great Pakhan.” 

As he finished this most peculiar letter, Dragunov's eyes shot wide open. 

“What the hell is this?” he calmly asked his secretary, setting the letter down carefully. 

“Well, sir, the courier told me he got it from a smiling man in a fur coat, but that's all I kn-” 

“Sounds like Jaba. Once a lousy gangster, always one, it seems,” Yevgeny interrupted. He got out of his chair and began to pace about his office. 

“Can't believe it. Those Yugrans signed a contract. Even thugs know how contracts work,” he muttered to himself, lighting another cigarette. After a few minutes of complaining and pondering, he  calmed himself down and looked out into his palace yard, where soldiers and workers were doing their job.  

“We'll find another deal. Hopefully, with some state less mercurial than that damnable Thief Territory,” thought Dragunov, out loud and to both himself and his secretary, “Not like they even ordered much, anyway.” His comment was met with silence for a while, but his old friend the secretary finally broke the silence. 

“Shot of vodka, sir?”
strings.YGR_initial.10.desc:
In the main hut of the pakhans, it was noisy as always. A thief was cleaning his pistols, someone was playing cards for cigarettes and another was sitting leaning on the back of a chair and smoking them. After several campaigns, raids and captures, everything was in the budget. But still, some kind of ghost of menace was wavering over them, the ghost of a dark past. The door creaked and began to open. Jaba Ioselani and his closest subordinates came in. Many abruptly got up from their chairs, others put out their cigarettes and continued to sit. But everyone understood that he was not with the best news. “Sit down, sit down. Don't be afraid. I have just one announcement, brothers. ” Everyone obeyed the order of the chief. A chair was brought to Jaba, he sat down and took off his military cap, took a cigarette with a match from someone sitting in the room and lit it. “Well, gentlemen, today is an important day. We're going on another raid.” Everyone smiled again, began to whisper, while Jaba looked at them with his menacing gaze. 

“It's not for the loot. We are going to Vorkuta, to the Gulags.” The noise of a fallen gun, and later a body. The Pakhans abruptly got up and saw the old prisoner Voron lying on the floor. He was having a seizure, many began to look for something near the bedside table. One of them went up to the lying Voron and opened a bottle of ammonia next to the nose of the fallen one. A minute passed, and there was more movement in the hut now than all the years before. Jaba was already standing over the awakened Voron with a cigarette in hand. 

The 60-year-old man had seen the Gulags under Bukharin, after the failure of the front and all the horrors of Vorkuta under Kaganovich, he wanted to say something to Jaba, but his voice clearly died down. Jaba, having extinguished his cigarette from the ashtray on the nightstand, called his subordinates, put on his cap and left the hut with them. Voron got up, sat down on the bed with the help of others. He looked around at the thieves looking anxiously, then at the door, then at himself. Voron took the gun again, loaded it and told everyone in the hut:
strings.YGR_initial.10.a: “I don't know about you, but i'm ready shoot some of Blokhin's cocksuckers.”
strings.YGR_initial.11.desc:
It was a normal morning in the camp when Yura and his team were ordered to go on what seemed to be a routine patrol. They were leaving that afternoon, the orders were clear, “scout the outskirts of Vorkuta, map out all guard posts and investigate for possible weak points in their lines”. 

When they set out from their camp Yura and his men were in a state of ecstasy, they were hoping for an exciting adventure. Some of them wondered how many men they could kill, or if they were going to see something at all. As time passed the grim reality of Siberia set in. 

As the sharp freezing winds embraced their bodies, they could only wonder when this would be over. Yura remembered easier times, remembered sitting by a campfire when he was younger, the stories of his father before the war. How would they sit by the chimney and escape the cruel winter. 

Yura hoped that this will be over soon so he could go back to camp and end this god forsaken mission.
strings.YGR_initial.12.desc:
Nestor sat out in the frozen prison yard, alone. Only about thirty or so men were even left alive here, excluding the fat, red-faced guards. This was probably the worst mission he'd ever been assigned to. 

Nestor Grigorovitch had been ordered to infiltrate the Vorkutan Rechlag, a camp relatively close to the border, in an attempt to find as much military intel as he could. Those military plans still eluded him, but right now, the mission was but one of his problems. 

In the Rechlag, there was little but filth, desolation, extreme temperatures, and starvation. When he got here a few months ago, men filled every cell; but all but 29 of them died making rifles, starved, were shot for fun, and died of disease. The worst part, however, was the warden's office.  

Next to his office, the warden ran what seemed to be some sort of medieval dungeon. Grigorovitch didn't know what was in there, but he did know how its victims sounded. The screams of pain weren't even the worst of it; what broke his heart was the begging. At least once a day, he'd hear frail, pained voices plead and beg not for their lives or for their freedom, but simply for the pain to end. Men would plead, and plead, promising to work harder, to eat less, anything for the torture to end. They almost always died. 

Nestor Grigorovitch needed to get out of here, but he needed to know what Blokhin was planning, first. Nestor had finally located the warden's official office. In between bouts of sadism, he was working with the Vorkuta Military Affairs Commission. The codger was sitting on months of top-secret military information. That afternoon, however, he had set aside a couple hours to help the warden do terrible things to a young Bashkir, leaving his office wide open. 

The wiry agent snuck past cell blocks and mess halls, inching closer to the door, even passing by the warden's quarters; the noises he heard shook him too close to the core, but he continued, finally reaching his target; an office full of intel. 

Nestor wasted no time grabbing everything he could hold; files, loose papers, anything of value to the Yugran military. As the Bashkir boy's screams filled his ears, he slinked back into the hallway, hands, shirt, pants, shoes, and underwear bulging with papers. In a moment of mad genius, the desperate agent decided to climb into the ventilation, crawling through nearly a kilometer of vent piping. After an hour of slowly making his way through boiling shafts, he found himself outside the building. Finally, he would be free! He ran through the same hole in the fence he had entered through, still not patched up by the guards, and left the gulag. 

Those pleading men would live on in him, as fuel for the destruction of this accursed place.
strings.YGR_initial.12.a: May God have mercy on us all.
strings.YGR_initial.13.desc:
Vasiliy Mikhailovich Blokhin, the Administrator, laid on the cold floor, his broken rib reverberating with painful pulses in his chest, his caved-in skull screeching with a migraine, his lips whispering obscenities, even when he had long lost the strength to stand, or even to shout, the hunger swallowing his innards. 

Those bastards. Those little bastards. Who gave THEM the right to even TOUCH him? These subhumans, these utter dregs of society, who were THEY to put him on trial? He had done no wrong-doing, no crime. It was no skin off his nose what these thrice-damned dogs had to think of him. If it were his call, each one of them would be back toiling in the GULAG! 

He served justice to them, all of them. So who were THEY to think that they had any right to serve this parody to him? 

The steel door of his cell opened with a whining creak, one of the guards peering in and giving Blokhin a couple of painful pokes with the barrel of his rifle. 

A voice sounded from behind the door, “He still up!?” 

The guard poked Blokhin again, a traitorous pained grunt escaping the Administrator's lungs. 

“Yeah,” The guard giggled drunkenly, “Well, a few more days without food and he'll certainly kick it!” Blokhin felt the boot slam into his side, his broken rib igniting with roaring agony, his voice rising to a pitiful shout. 

“Good night, Papasha! Don't keep the reaper waiting!” The guard laughed, the sound of his boots disappearing behind the steel door, leaving Blokhin alone with his enraged thoughts.
strings.YGR_initial.13.a: Justice... In one form or another
strings.YGR_initial.14.desc:
Lazar Kaganovich had once been a name that struck fear across the Urals. The entire state of Tyumen swore loyalty exclusively to him, and his orders were followed by all. His people could never fall, for they believed in true communism. That was the case, until the Thief Territory proved him wrong. 

Yugra had thoroughly destroyed his nation, and his government was now dead or in custody. Kaganovich himself was being led away from his cell in solitary confinement; a horrible little closet full of mold, rat dung, and other filth. 

The communist dream would seemingly end here in this “courthouse” -- a jury-rigged holding-cell-turned-courtroom assembled in an empty hall of the prison where he would surely see his end. His jailers roughly dragged the former General Secretary to the “dock” -- a wooden chair that he was promptly handcuffed to. 

He had no expectation that the trial would be fair. 

Just as the Yugrans had done with other state-endings, the biggest thief of them all was there to pass the sentence himself. 

“Lazar Kaganovich, you have been found guilty of murder and treason against the Thief Territory. Your sentence is death.” A bullet went through his mouth before he could open it. 

Shortly afterwards, Nikita Khruschev, another member of the Kaganovich government, was dragged into the block and handcuffed to the same blood-stained chair.  

“Friends, friends, I'm sure there's a misunderstanding here. Obviously, old Lazar was a traitor, but surely we can settle this on neutral gr-” Khruschev came out swinging, but was quickly shut down by Ioseliani. 

“We are not open to negotiations, Mr. Khrushchev.  We are interested only in your death.” 

Khruschev, seeing that his end was here, relented. 

“...I'd prefer an open casket, if that's alright.”
strings.YGR_initial.15.desc:
The Great Trial is now a pipe dream. Yazov has failed to destroy Germany and avenge Russia. Yazov, the great leader of the Black League now disheveled was a shell of his former shelf. He failed to defeat a rabble of mere gangsters and thugs. This was an embarrassment for the hardened and ultra-militaristic Black League. 

Now Yazov and his loyal officers were at the mercy of Yugra's Gangsters in the ruins of Omsk. Many of Yazov's fellow officers were defiant at the gangsters even at gunpoint, yelling obscenities and insults at their captors. Yazov however accepted his fate. 

Ioseliani who is observing his men with the captured Black League leadership gestures his men to take Yazov to him and execute the others. The men oblige taking Yazov to him, while the others are forcibly lined up to a wall and gunned down. 

“You know, I admire your resolve and dedication.” Ioseliani says, impressed by the Black League and their zeal in fighting their enemies. “.....” Yazov says nothing, clearly distraught at the defeat of the Black League and how the Great Trial will never happen. “Hey, don't give me that look. Maybe in another life I lose, and you succeed.” 

“Just kill me. I can't live with this failure.” The defeated Glavkoverkh states. Ioseliani obliges and unholsters his TT-33. At the same time, he takes out of pack of cigarettes. “Cigarette?” Ioseliani offers handing Yazov a cigarette. 

Yazov reaches it out with his hand.
strings.YGR_initial.16.desc:
The two men stared at each other closely, seemingly looking into the other's eyes as if they were trying to read their thoughts.  General Pavel Batov looked at the letter in his hands.  The “Great Pakhan” sitting in front of him was demanding his surrender before war had even properly started. 

“Mister Ioseliani...” 

“You will address me as Great Pakhan” 

“I will do no such thing.  We sit here today as equals.  You have asked for my submission.  You offer me mercy and say that our men will have a chance for glory.  But the men of the Third Army do not wish for glory and money.  What is there to steal in this impoverished land, but from our own people?  The Red Army only has one purpose: to serve Russia, no matter the cost.”  

“General Batov, I urge you to reconsider.  We are not the bandit rabble that you believe us to be.  The Bratva is just that, a brotherhood.  We are not merely a mafia, not merely another petty fiefdom.  And any thief worth his honor will die for the Bratva without a second thought.  Your choice is simple.  We will crush your Red Army one way or another.  Whether you outlive it is up to you.”“ 

Batov thought:
strings.YGR_initial.17.desc:
The noise shook the bar. The “soldiers” drank and sang. The girls danced on the tables with the guys. The gang leaders were discussing business at a separate table. Among them were Usoyan, Ioselani and others. 

“There are very nice bunkers in Omsk. Can we use it as headquarters?” “Surely, there are some weapons there. We'll search, find and sell, maybe to these Frenchmen or whoever they are” said Usoyan, drinking another glass. “Alright, gentlemen, I'm going outside” 

Jaba leaved the building, lit a cigarette and began to look around. Dark starry city night. Right in front of him was a residential neighborhood built up under Bukharin. There were lights on in the windows, but the streets were empty. A small Soviet town and it is in his power. Ioselani took another pull. He remembered the Gulags, he remembered Blokhin, he remembered the rigid prison system. But now, he is the king of this system. He rules everything. And he can do more. Thoughts of greatness invigorated Jaba. Through the thorns to the stars. From dirt to princes. From nothing to everything. Jaba took several deep puffs of his cigarette again. 

After finishing smoking, he threw the butt away near the entrance to the bar, adjusted his cap, checked his gun and went into the bar again. It's time to celebrate properly to get back to business again.
strings.YGR_initial.18.desc:
The trucks rode on down the empty road, the sounds of wheels against gravel and snow the only sound that pierced the dead of night.  The bandits inside were cleaning their weapons, getting ready for the battle that was to come.  For too long, their commander had thought, had his bandit company limited themselves to small-scale raids.  This time, they would perform their biggest heist yet: taking out an entire supply depot of Rokossovsky's 3rd Army.  The large amount of weapons would surely fetch a handsome price in Yugra's Black Market.  Perhaps, the Pakhan himself might notice him, but Grisha chuckled at the thought of that Georgian bastard ever noticing anyone but the ladies of the night 

 His thoughts were interrupted by the screeching of brakes.  “Everyone out!  Let's go!  Blow the gate and let's get the machine guns set up!”  The soldiers rushed out of the trucks, blasting their submachine guns at the guard posts.  Grisha stepped out of the vehicle, hoping to lead his men to glory.  His dreams were ended by a single well-placed bullet from a Red Army sniper. 

  The bandits tried to flee back to their trucks, but most were cut down by machine gun fire from the outpost's experienced men.  Where there should have been cries of celebration and pride, Grisha's Bandits found only the cries of pain and death.
strings.YGR_initial.19.desc:
General Pavel Shiryaev had been sleeping for the longest he had slept in weeks; approximately six hours. A dreamless sleep, but sleep nonetheless. Unfortunately, a knock at the door that cold early morning awoke him abruptly. 

“Sir, there's something you're going to want to see here!” his secretary shouted from behind the door. With a grumble, Shiryaev got up out of his chair and opened the door. 

“There's some strange news from the Yugran border, sir,” said the secretary, as he handed the general a yellow folder, “From what the courier told me, some of our men just attacked the thieves' forts.” With a creased look on his face, Pavel took the folder, walked over to his desk, and sat down. He began reviewing the files; the events took place just that night, with what looked to be rogue Zlatoust soldiers. Pictures showed them wearing... was that his army's ensignia? Was his army disobeying him, now? He continued reading. The soldiers had stormed upwards of twenty Yugran forts and emplacements, technically pushing the border forwards about half a kilometer. Were it ordered, it would have been a massive victory for Zlatoust; weakening the border on the Yugra side while the Republic gained land and forts. However, something was still off to the general. 

As he kept reading, Shiryaev began noticing some strange anomalies, even with the fact that it wasn't even ordered notwithstanding; most of the men were using much older weapons than what Zlatoust was issuing to its soldiers, with many of the guns looking fresh out of Vorkuta. Furthermore, in at least three of the raids, some soldiers simply walked over to the fort, hung up the Zlatoust flag, and walked over to the next fort. The behavior of these supposed Zlatoust soldiers simply did not line up with how they were trained, and the rather gruff appearance of the soldiers would be downright insulting to see, if he actually was their general. 

There was only one viable conclusion he could make; they were not his men. They were, quite clearly, Yugran forces who had faked an international incident to incite war between the two nations. Action had to be taken. He looked over to his secretary, a particularly literate and fast-learning lieutenant, and issued the first order of this new war; 

“Lieutenant!  Call the majors, call every officer, call the field marshall! We need to mobilize at the Yugra border, immediately!”
strings.YGR_initial.20.desc:
Batov sighed as he looked at Ioseliani, the Great Pakhan grinning back at the General. 

“So, what do we have here, hm? No more uniform-clad lads to throw at me?” Ioseliani swigged from his bottle, chuckling. 

Batov clenched and unclenched his fists, his expression darkening. “I will not let you rule these people, you damned scum. This is all a farce, a disgusting farce.” 

Ioseliani listened carefully, placing the bottle down next to the table leg and observing Batov with an interested look. “You surprise me, old boy.” 

Batov lips turned into a thin line.

“Blokhin cursed me because I was a bandit. Dragunov never intended to continue working with me, to him I was a useful hammer to swing around at his possible enemies. The bitches in the Free Aviators just had nothing to fight back with. But you?” 

Ioseliani chuckled. “You are lead by 'THE PEOPLE'?” 

Batov lifted his eyes, his jaw clenched. “Yes. In the end, I shall serve the Russian people, because that is what the military is for, damn it. Not for kicking people down, not for terrifying them into submission, it is to protect them. And I will not let scum like you suck the lifeblood out of the nation...” 

Ioseliani listened, before going quiet and looking to the side, scratching his bearded cheek, “You're a weird one, you are. HAH! I suppose we can work with that!” The Great Pakhan sat forward, staring the General in the eye. “A thief's word means a lot in this world, old boy. I promise to work for 'THE PEOPLE', if you work for me. We need the expertise after all.” 

Batov sighed, looking away. Ioseliani picked up the bottle and stood from the table. 

“I'll give you time to think, old-” 

Batov interrupted.
strings.YGR_initial.21.desc:
“Is this thing on? Hello? Testing, one, two... Oh, we're on!” 

“Good morning, thieves-in-law! You're listening to Radio Yugorsk. I'm your host, George Kennan, and can I just say how great it is to be out of that camp! You were all there, you know it was bad, but now we're free! Free as America! And I can tell you that, I'm from out there. Anyways, here's what's on the board for today. 

”From the capital, we have big news! The second meeting of the bosses has finally been convened, after months, if not years of waiting! There's a lot at stake here, if you don't know; this meeting might just decide all of our fates. Of course, personally, I'm just happy to not be squatting in a camp, but I know a few anonymous folks among us that care about what's gonna happen next. 

“Now, our most likely course of action is that we go and shoot Blokhin and his boys, which is personally my favorite course of action. However, and I do mean however, not all of us are gonna come back from that. We're relatively evenly matched; they've got discipline, and we've got energy. When we're out shooting those commie bastards, make sure you hit them in the head; it'll get 'em to the lake of fire sooner. 

”Of course, there's still some stuff to do around the house. They're rebuilding the old airport, sending the flyboys out there and all. Plus, we could always have a few more guns.“ 

”However, and I do mean however, a little birdie told me that there's something going on up at the top. Something with two people who don't like each other very much. Now, there's not much information to share about it, and even less that I'm at liberty to share, but my advice to you is this;
strings.YGR_initial.22.t: A Hideout Full of Good Loot
strings.YGR_initial.22.d:
The “Jaguars” squad, part of the Prestupnaya Diviziya, would occasionally carry out raids on weaker neighbors. This was how they spent their free time, while also lining their pockets and funding themselves, which made them a self-sufficient combat unit. However, as is often the case, no matter how much loot criminal groups acquire, it's never enough - and this applies to military units of this type as well. Consequently, it's only natural that they were among the few brigades that seriously volunteered to take part in the first large-scale raid on the territory of the Ural Military District.

In a small section of the raid, 10 kilometers deep, two former inmates and friends - nicknamed “Shestyorka” and “Gosha” - had gathered. These were obviously not their real names, but over the years of such a turbulent life, they had grown accustomed to them. At first, the District's border guards put up a brief fight, hoping for reinforcements from other directions, which were delayed by a lightning-fast raid by other neighboring criminal units. An hour into the firefight, the border post surrendered its weapons and was taken prisoner. In addition, to the surprise of both sides, a basement was discovered in the border guards' small, single-story building, which appeared to have been intended as a bomb shelter.

However, inside, the two robbers discovered something incredible - a stockpile of provisions, and in particular, moonshine along with several dozen bottles of vodka (which hadn't even been used by the other enemy garrisons!). They immediately reported this “crystal-clear” bottles to the entire brigade's command and requested urgent reinforcements. Without wasting a minute, while “Shestyorka” was alerting their superiors, “Gosha” opened the first 1-liter bottle of vodka he could find and began chugging it straight from the bottle, without even a snack. When he finished his call, he turned to his comrade, who, it seemed, had already downed half the bottle, and sighed deeply.

“Ahh, I just knew I shouldn't have let you go first to check the supplies we'd gotten! You should've had the decency to offer me some, damn it. Well, the other guys will be here in about an hour, so I'll grab a bottle for myself too, heh-heh.”

Without exaggeration, this was definitely their happiest day in the last year. And since the brigade's superiors hadn't yet been informed of the exact amount of alcohol found or the size of this basement stash, the two slackers decided to quickly “celebrate” this relatively simple victory and the discovery of this find.
strings.YGR_initial.23.t: A Failure of Our Audacious Thieving Raid
strings.YGR_initial.23.d:
The “Jaguars” squad, part of the Prestupnaya Diviziya, would occasionally carry out raids on weaker neighbors. This was how they spent their free time, while also lining their pockets and funding themselves, which made them a self-sufficient combat unit. However, as is often the case, no matter how much loot criminal groups acquire, it's never enough - and this applies to military units of this type as well. Consequently, it's only natural that they were among the few brigades that seriously volunteered to take part in the first large-scale raid on the territory of the Ural Military District.

In a small section of the raid, 10 kilometers deep, two former inmates and friends - nicknamed “Shestyorka” and “Gosha” - had gathered. These were obviously not their real names, but over the years of such a turbulent life, they had grown accustomed to them. At first, everything went according to their plan, as the enemy didn't significantly outnumber them. However, after half an hour of continuous firefights, a truck packed with about two dozen reinforcements from the garrison pulled onto the battlefield. “Shestyorka” was the first to spot this, and he turned to his comrade.

“Fucking cat, Gosha, the enemy has received reinforcements, and ours guys won't be here anytime soon! It's too late for us to retreat together - we're only 30 meters from their positions! This is a mess - give me all the grenades you have; I'll throw them and fire to kill to distract them, while you retreat to our guys!”

“Gosha” understood the danger and handed all four of his grenades to his friend. Although they'd known each other for three years, they'd become close friends during that time - but his own life was still far more valuable than any loot. He began to run, dodging bullets by ducking into the bushes, when a few seconds later he heard explosions, one after another. After running 100 meters away, he saw a blown-up car and a single-story border guard house engulfed in a massive blaze. He couldn't believe that two or three grenades could have caused such a fire, and from then on, he could only speculate about what had led to such an intense blaze.
strings.YGR_initial.23.a: “Damn, they didn't prepare me for dangerous run-ins like this in prison!”
strings.YGR_initial.24.t: Repelling a Sudden Raid by Northern Bandits
strings.YGR_initial.24.a: Those thieves and gangsters finally got what they deserved!
strings.YGR_initial.25.t: A Successful Sudden Raid by the Northern Bandits
strings.YGR_initial.25.a: This bitter defeat will affect our morale in the coming months.
strings.YGR_news.1.desc:
Against all odds, the Thieves in Law of Yugra have descended from their territories in the frigid north of Russia to take the entire region of West Siberia. Though outnumbered from the start, the thieves fought, tricked, and bribed their way from prisoners to rulers. So far, we know little about the peculiar state and its future.

However, today the “Great Pakhan” of the newly declared “West Siberian Thief Territory,” a Georgian by the name of Jaba Ioseliani has announced that the Thieves ultimately hope to reunify all of Russia and become its protectors and saviors. Already, they have begun to open their borders to trade. It seems they are hoping to make a great deal of money in their new positions.
strings.YGR_news.2.desc:
Unexpected news has come from Russia today, as the embattled, continent-stretching land finally turns a new page in its scarred history. Apparently, a government consisting entirely of Russian mafia bosses has taken control of the nation in a decade-spanning bid to unify Russia despite the harsh odds they faced, allegedly beginning their struggle as mere escapees from the frigid gulags of Vorkuta, its prisoners left to rot in the aftermath of the Soviet Union's fall.

Under the Georgian ex-convict Jaba Ioseliani, the new Russian state, calling itself the “Thief Territory”, will run a country in a way never before seen on Earth: a state for and by the people, but especially those that are criminals. Only time will tell what sort of place Russia will become, and what this rather surprising. unique, and quite honestly concerning turn of events means for the rest of the world.
strings.YGR_news.2.a: From scum to the saviours of Russia
strings.YGR_news.3.desc:
Incredible news has arrived from Russia today. After 30 years following their defeat against the Third Reich, the Russians stand united once more. Of all the petty warlords that dotted the vast territory of Siberia, the ex bandit and now the de facto leader of Russia, a Kurdish by the name of Aslan Usoyan, has announced the subjugation of all rivals to his state.

The most peculiar detail of the new overlord of Russia is his form of government. Having couped his former rival, Jaba Ioseliani, Usoyan has transformed the once anarchic Thief Territory into an immense corporation controlling the majority of the products sold in the new Russia, while offering cheap labor and loose regulations. Companies and directors around the world are celebrating the new state.
strings.YGR_news.3.a: It's a good day to be a capitalist
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.0.desc:
The cracks are forming, the divisions have begun. 

Jaba Ioselani, the Great Pakhan, the visionary, the man of the people, the military man. His men are in the top rungs, his officers are in the military, their names are on plaques and official lists. The crown rests on his head as his tendrils sneak through the land, tying everything back to him. The Georgian Wolf, his fangs grasping region to region, trying to hold his allies together with a sure but loose grip. Idealists love him, pragmatists tolerate him, the average vor v zakone respects him. 

There will be a place for all gangsters... if they have the wit or strength for it. 

On the other hand, Aslan Ûsoyan, the businessman, knows his truth: the Thief and the civvie can never be equal. The Kurdish Spider's financial webs have been built up through the regions, each vibration of his business's webbing giving Aslan more and more confidence in his power. If Ioselani wants each gang on its own, Aslan shall have their powers under him. If Ioselani wants civilians to join the ranks, Aslan will not tolerate the farm animal joining the farmer. 

If everyone is a thief, no one is.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.1.desc:
The Great Pakhan stared boredly at the gun barrels pointed at him, Usoyan entering his office behind the group of soldiers that came in first. 

“It's over,” Usoyan noted, his hands interlocked behind his back. “Jaba, no one's coming.” 

Ioseliani yawned demonstratively. “No one, as in-” 

“No one. Your men are all gone. Surrender.” Usoyan responded almost mechanically. 

Ioseliani would sigh and stand up from his armchair, ignoring the clicks of the rifles pointed at him. 

“I got a weapon.”  

Usoyan blinked at the Great Pakhan's statement, “Pardon?” 

“I got a weapon,” Ioseliani smirked at the soldiers' change in demeanour, many getting nervous and grasping their rifles tighter. 

“No, you don't...” Usoyan could generally see where this was going. 

“Oh yes, I do! I got a weapon! I got a-!” Suddenly, Ioseliani's hand would dart into his jacket's inside pocket. 

BANG! BANG! BANG! 

The Great Pakhan fell back, sagging into his armchair, the blood beginning to mix with the whisky seeping from the bullet hole in the flask he reached into his jacket for. 

Usoyan grimaced as the soldiers lowered their rifles. “What a fucking mess...”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.2.desc:
For a day so bright and sunny, it was awfully cold in Aslan's prison cell. Not that he would know, of course. 

The moment it was clear that Aslan Usoyan was not going to win out in his little power struggle with Ioseliani, he, alongside the last remaining pakhans on his side, were rounded up and thrown in a Tyumen jailhouse. Usoyan himself had been sitting in a rotting cell for about four hours, after being abducted earlier that morning. He was still wearing his suit. 

As Usoyan tried and failed to figure out what exactly went wrong, and how Jaba had managed to pull off such a maneuver, the lock on his cell was fiddled with, then finally hit several times, before finally being unlocked. The door opened, letting in quite a bit of sunlight from holes in the bombed-out jail's roof, which blinded Usoyan momentarily. Once his eyes adjusted, he was met with an odd, but not altogether surprising sight; just as he had been there to see the ends of his foreign opponents, Jaba Ioseliani himself had come to end this conflict once and for all. 

“Aslan, young boy!” Jaba greeted his rival, with a smile, “Looks like you've lost this one.” Ioseliani picked Usoyan up off of the squalid floor and pulled him out of the cell. His smile faded, and, with a stern gaze Aslan had never seen on the man, led the man through the halls of the old jail. 

When the two of them finally left the building, Aslan could barely contain his horror; every single one of his co-conspirators, a list hundreds of people long, had been lined up along the side of the jail. From the looks of it, an entire Yugran battalion was there, too, Kalashnikovs at the ready. The end had finally come for their plans. 

Usoyan was put at the end of the line, closest to the entrance, where he stood next to a stout man in thug's clothes. Looking at him, as well as many of the other men in the line, Usoyan realized that he didn't even know most of these people. Yet, here they were, about to die for him. Once everyone was firmly in line, Ioseliani ordered his men to line up across from the prisoners, with one soldier to every captive. The “Load!”, “Prime!”, and “Ready!” orders came a lot faster than Usoyan was hoping for, but it was an awfully long time before he heard “Fire!”. 

As the bullet went through his head, his last thoughts were of his mother.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.3.desc:
“Gazmanov?” “Fuck 'em.” 

“Kamchatski?” “Fuck 'em.” 

“Abasdze?” “Fuck 'em.” 

Ioseliani threw a knife, hitting a perfect bulls-eye on the dart-board, while Rafael read off the names of Usoyan's cronies and noted down the 'death orders' that the Great Pakhan pronounced as easily as he pronounced a swear. 

“You sure about Abasdze?”  

Ioseliani paused as he took out another knife, turning to his right-hand man with a disgruntled expression. 

“Now, why would I be unsure, Raf, hm?” 

Rafael gulped, “I didn't mean anything behind it, just saying, the guy has connections to the Georgian-” 

Ioseliani cut Rafael off with a lifted hand, “Raf, I said we are going snake hunting, right?” 

“R-right...” 

“Well then, why are you giving this so much fucking thought, hm? Sure, a snake can be a very good decoration, especially if it's exotic, but why should I keep a venomous son of a bitch and risk getting bit when I can tear the fucker's head off!? HM!? RAF!” 

The right-hand man gave a nervous huff. “L-look, all I'm saying, we shouldn't go full Bukharin on this. Y'know, let's not shoot ourselves in the leg just because they don't align with us-” 

“It's a war, Raf, and there's no quarter given or taken. Now, either man the fuck up and keep reading, or get the fuck out.” Ioseliani turned back to the dartboard, flicking another knife at it, the blade hitting the hilt of the previous dagger and bouncing off. 

The Great Pakhan continued, “We leave one Usoyan crony, he'll sprout two more, two will turn into four, and soon his business bullshit will be all over us again.” 

“...” 

“So? Continue!” 

“Right, Ibrahem?”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.5.desc:
“The Far East metal? That's all they want?” Usoyan hummed a little. “The Japanese are certainly cheap.” 

Ilo stood near his commander, side-eyeing the contracts they had received in huge bundles, the Kurdish Spider now having sat for several hours, staring over the demands that came with the aid. 

“Well...” Usoyan stamped the document, one of many dozen he had already gone through. “Their equipment will carry us if ours won't.” 

Ilo cleared his throat. “Maybe take a look at the American letters? I think that there were a few quite simple ones.”  

“Certainly, certainly.” Usoyan pulled one of the sheets, before snorting and taking out a blank piece of paper and writing something on it. 

“Sir?” 

Usoyan handed the two sheets back to Ilo, chuckling. “There, send them this. It should work.” 

“If it isn't too much, what exactly-” 

“Oh, nothing actually impactful,”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.6.desc:
Rafael felt a sense of deja vu, sighing as he read off the new list of names, noting down Ioseliani's new orders. 

“Gurgenidze...” 

“Hmmmmm... Minister of the Interior.” 

“Voronov...” 

“Ah, that prick, stick him into the Ministry of Agriculture, somewhere at the bottom. Let's make him eat shit.” 

“Dekanosidze...” 

“Well, he's quite a good officer. I think he deserves a good time in Financing.” Ioseliani, who had up to then been leaning back in his chair, would sit forward and stretch, yawning. 

Rafael looked at the time. “It is quite late in the night, Jaba. Maybe we should finish tomorrow.” 

Ioseliani lifted his eyes in a tired manner, “Right, gimme a run-down of the remaining candidates.” 

Rafael quickly eyed the list. “Some Georgians who sided with you over Usoyan and a Russian officer who crossed lines and flipped to our side.” 

The Great Pakhan stood from his seat, picking up the bottle on the table and headed towards the exit, “Stuff them somewhere in the Military Office and the Russian can go into Agricultural low-levels as well.” 

Rafael blinked, pronouncing nervously, “Jaba, maybe we should rethink this... are we not rushing things?” 

Ioseliani turned his head, the door to the dark outside already opened, giving his right-hand man a disgruntled look, “Well, if they're gonna be loyal,”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.6.a: “Who gives a shit where they are?”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.7.desc:
Within the interlocking mechanisms and struggles of the Thief State, the resistance between Great Pakhan Ioseliani and Aslan Usoyan have exploded! A recent caravan of Usoyan supply-runners has disappeared for several days. Upon mounting a search, the trucks and the bodies of the drivers were found, or rather, whatever remained of them. From the official investigation, it is known that the caravan has been attacked mid-drive, all of the drivers that survived the initial attack were executed by bayonets, and the trucks were found to have been emptied before the attackers got away. 

The event has caused an uproar within the Circle, many accusing Ioseliani's forces of a lack of oversight over his men and some even accusing the Great Pakhan of giving a direct order for the assault, while many others blame Usoyan for a possible false flag operation, considering the light load of the trucks compared to the usual transports or a possible assault on the Thief's army as many drivers were found to be armed.
