strings.YGR_powerstruggle.7.a: No one is innocent, everyone is guilty...
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.8.desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 11:14 PM; 

This month's financial report has had an unfortunate discovery; multiple high-level bureaucrats and underlings have started to receive considerable amounts of money from obfuscated accounts. Further investigation revealed the accounts to secretly belong to various accountants and analysts in the employ of Aslan Usoyan. The accounts have been shut down, but there isn't enough evidence to arrest anyone, and it won't be long before they simply open new accounts. 

OPINION: Usoyan's webs seem to be more intricate than we previously believed. Although we delayed them from paying out our men in the name of getting them on Aslan's side, you can probably guess this won't stop them very much at all. Us Kurds have to be crafty to survive, these days, but Usoyan seems to supersede “crafty” with moves like these. We have to get a grip on our men if we want to stay in power. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.8.a: Start an investigation, we need to uncover everything.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.9.desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 6:41 PM; 

 After a routine inspection, several more thieves-in-law than before were found with documents, pins, and other pieces of evidence suggesting that they are loyal to our rival, Aslan Usoyan. It appears a series of bribes, threats, and ideological conversions continue to move our men under Usoyan's thrall. Counteraction is recommended at this time. 

OPINION: “Usoyan got the drop on us; more of our underlings and officials have gone to his side. If we want to end this power struggle, we need to keep everyone we can on our side, not let our opponents steal people right from under our noses. I know I'm meant to be your informant, but it doesn't bring me much confidence to see these sorts of things happen.” 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Mr. Usoyan's secretary as of writing this, 

Leonid Rojov
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.9.a: Blackmail everyone involved, I won't surround myself with snakes.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.10.desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

Last night, Aslan Usoyan's underlings posted up hundreds of posters throughout several of out major cities; posters either painting Aslan as a hero of the people whose reforms would make Russia great, or condemning Jaba Ioseliani as a complacent, greedy man who wishes to steal from the Russian people. Although the veracity of these posters is, at the very least, up for debate, thousands of people have seen it, and only a couple dozen have been vandalized or taken down in response. 

OPINION: Although it is difficult to gauge the popularity of political posters, especially in an environment where many are scared of those that put them up, just how many of them are still up, as well as the more likely still being put up, makes this move a resounding success on the part of Usoyan. The time to make our own move comes closer and closer, and our move must be swift and a bit more than decisive. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.10.a: Tear everything down, no more people should see this.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.11.desc:
Extract from 'Utro' Gazette: 

...while investigation into the incident is still on-going, several gunmen have been wounded during the attack on {ILLEGIBLE} Square. Several dozen bystanders were caught in the fire of the terrorists, including women and children. The city has been put under lockdown. The editorials condolences go out to the families of the victims...
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.12.desc:
Extract from armed forces radio chatter, dated *REDACTED*: 

*Alpha04*: We've checked, there's nothing in this part of town, the reports you got are bullshit. 

*Base*: Team Alpha, continue investi- 

*Alpha04*: *sounds of gunfire* *ILLEGIBLE* 

*Base*: Team Alpha, Team Alpha, respond! What is your situation!? 

*Alpha04*: Shit, shit, they've got us pincered! Base, we'll need ba- *RADIO STATIC* *ILLEGIBLE* 

Contact with Team Alpha lost.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.13.desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

Yesterday morning, Usoyan was seen making a public appearance, a considerable crowd of people was listening to his speech. Promises of freedom, wealth and greatness were made by the Kurd, making a huge part of those in attendance flock to his banner, or cease support of our power base. 

OPINION: Well, there's nothing too special about this move, the best we can do is answer by heading our own public campaign, and considering your charisma, it shouldn't be too difficult of a task. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.13.a: You have a point, I'll schedule a public meeting in three days.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.14.desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

These last days our spies detected an influx of anomalous investments from foreign businessmen into Thief subsidiaries. After some digging, we managed to track down the sudden source of liquidity, the capital was passed to façade companies whose owners were only name bearers. Upon further investigation and “convincing” of the company holders, we discovered that most of these shells track back to Usoyan. Wherever that funding goes is not certain, but it doesn't look like it's beneficial to the state apparatus.

OPINION: Sir, this is proof that our economic laws are flawed, these evident loopholes can be used by enemies of the state to smuggle in funds from outside our territory. We could make use for some regulation.

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.14.a: Raise the security, foreign investments are to be double-checked.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.15.desc:
Yesterday the Great Pakhan guard has warned that there was a breach of security in the military outpost *REDACTED*. As of now, we were able to confirm that the perpetrators stole the frequencies and ciphers that the military uses for communications. We do not know exactly how much the Usoyani loyalists managed to gain from our conversations, but all communications for the several weeks are to be considered compromised and the ciphers are to be re-written. 

OPINION: “Now THIS will prove to be a real problem, sir. The best course of action is to cut all communications on the leaked frequencies and remake our cipher books. At least for the coming week, I believe our command structure is partially paralysed.”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.16.desc:
Today, a potential attack on our installation on *REDACTED* street has been preemptively halted, with the effort of several officers and back-up patrols all the assailants were either arrested or disposed of. Most of the signs and the accounts we were to beat out of the arrested point to this being organised by Usoyan. This failure will likely discredit him, at least for the time being. 

OPINION: “A close shave, a very close one, we should higher the security of *REDACTED* just to be safe. Considering that the weapons generally match some of those missing 'in transport' from factories, I also suggest to investigate the state apparatus further.”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.17.desc:
Extract from “Utro” Gazette: 

A recent speech by famed business magnate Aslan Usoyan has come under fire from both the Circle and the general public. While having his speech dismissed in the Circle as 'babble', the reaction to the same speech was much more violent from the people in the streets as Mister Usoyan was pelted with rocks, only with the arrival of the local security forces ending the violent attack.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.18.desc:
SITREP: 06:03 

Reports have come in from several of our contacts that last night, no less than two dozen men sympathetic, if not loyal, to our cause were taken forcibly from their homes, put on a bus, and taken out to a forest outside Tyumen, where they were apparently lined up and shot. At least one of our contacts was forced to shoot several men, many of whom knew him as an ally. Our popular support is already starting to stagnate as news of this event spreads. 

OPINION: Really? Just... taken and shot? Like dogs? This sort of thing cannot happen again if we want even one person to work with us. ...By the way, you should really read these Mario Fusco books. You could learn a lot from the main character; for example, he wouldn't let his friends be rounded up like cattle. 

SIGNED: Your loyal secretary and countryman, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.19.desc:
SITREP: 14:45 

This morning, the Jaba Ioseliani government held several meetings, where pakhans not aligned with us were shown “the stability of the government, and how Ioseliani was a good leader”, and whatnot. The meetings also either dissuaded or “dissuaded” them from working with us. Due to the apparent success of these meetings, several pakhans and officials have either left our circles or cut off recruitment contact. 

OPINION: It appears Ioseliani figured out how to stabilize the government, or at least convince people the government is stable. This tactic has already lost us some good men, and we need to step up our efforts if we want any hope of victory. 

SIGNED: Your loyal secretary and countryman, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.19.a: Prepare as many propaganda posters as possible, we need to recover our lost base
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.20.desc:
Extract from armed forces radio chatter, dated *REDACTED*: 

**Omega 5**: “Base, the target's on the move, I think he caught on we're coming.” 

**Base**: “You are free to engage him ASAP, Omega.” 

**Omega 5**: “There are civvies around-” 

**Base**: “You are free to engage, the capture of the internal threat is more important.” 

**Omega 5**: “Understood, engaging the target.”
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.21.desc:
“All shall be well! And it shall be well forever!” 

In essence, Raf thought that was all of his Boss's speeches. At least when he spoke about himself.  

The assistant eyed the crowd nervously, the burning sea of enthusiasm boiling with ripples and waves as men and women, young and old, all focused their eyes on the Great Pakhan standing victoriously on the podium. 

The speeches all felt the same, but in the end, Raf considered...
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.22.desc:
Extract from 'Utro' Gazette: 

On the morning of *ILLEGIBLE* several pakhans, their aides and gang constituencies were found to have been arrested! This has sparked outrage in the Circle as many speculate a fear of returnal to Bukharinist practices of silencing the opposition or the attack on the independence and autonomy of the Pakhans, chief among them being Aslan Usoyan. The Great Pakhan's administration has refused to comment, citing 'internal affairs' among the Circle.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.23.desc:
Snippet of exchange of Officer *REDACTED* from *REDACTED*: 

Spectre, Ghostly, Omega, congratulations gentlemen. It seems our higher ups have either recognised our achievements or signed the wrong check, because more equipment is coming our way. I believe that the 'assessment' of our targets will be going more smoothly from now on. Cashmere, out.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.23.a: Eyes in every corner, ear in every wall...
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.24.desc:
SITREP: 21:03; 

Since 14:00 yesterday evening, 17 of our contacts, both already embedded within Jaba Ioseliani's incompetent regime and in the process of being recruited, were arrested in a Bolshevik-esque purge. Apparently, one of Ioseliani's inspectors discovered our correspondence with these contacts in a random mailroom bust, which was quickly reported to the regime's secret police. 

OPINION: We've been talking to our guys through the mail? Really? Well, it could have been worse; they could have gotten the actually effective ones. I recommend switching how we correspond with contacts as well as ensuring their loyalty. Silly mistakes like this will keep us out of power forever, if not killed.  

SIGNED: Your loyal secretary and countryman, 

Leonid Rojov.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.24.a: Cover our tracks, we need damage control.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.25.desc:
Raf took a step back as several of the crowd tried to approach the podium, screaming angrily. 

Whatever Ioseliani had just mentioned in his speech did not seem to calm the crowd, instead it only got worse. 

“S-sir, I think it's better-” Raf leaned out of the way of the flying rock. “Sir! Let's go!” 

Maybe the speeches were all the same, but this time it didn't seem to work.
strings.YGR_powerstruggle.26.desc:
Extract from armed forces radio chatter, dated *REDACTED*: 

**Sigma 3**: “Shit, Base, we lost him. The bastard disappeared.” 

**Base**: “There is too much on the line, continue the search, the perimeter should be secured, he has nowhere to go.” 

**Sigma 3**: “Affirma-” 

**Beta 9**: “Base, we're being lit up here! The perimeter has been compromised, I REPEAT, THE PERIMETER HAS BEEN-” *Static* 

**Base**: “Sigma, the mission has been compromised, exfiltrate ASAP.” 

**Sigma 3**: “Sometimes I really fucking hate this job...”
strings.YGR_regional.0.d:
Since the small circle of people close to Pahan had full access to the outside world, not counting the majority of the country's isolated civilian population, interesting information was obtained from Asia. The recently formed Malaysian state, which rose from under Japanese influence and gained independence as a result of a brutal war, is gradually opening up to the world. Some American diplomatic channels have been reporting for the past two months on the Malaysian government's willingness to cede some control over its natural resources to investors in exchange for assistance in industrialization.

The Americans were, of course, the first to respond, taking indirect control of the resource-rich capital city of Kuala Lumpur. We, of course, do not have as many resources as the leading OFN state, but we do have something to offer in exchange. In exchange for our equipment and several large civilian enterprises located in Tyumen, we will gain a valuable trading partner, while receiving the rubber that Russia so desperately needs. We need it for the production of combat aircraft, but on paper and in official documentation, this rubber will be used exclusively for civilian purposes. Who knows, maybe this work will turn into something more in the future?
strings.YGR_regional.2.desc:
A gang of bandits rushed to the hall. They were carrying expensive liquor, most of them already drunk after looting and drinking most of the alcohol they found in an old warehouse. 

 As they sat down they sat in a large dining hall, the realization of their achievement set in. They wondered how a conqueror would celebrate such an occasion. A feast! The old Nikolai shouted. He remembered hearing stories of old kings holding massive feast for important events. 

The men agreed, they wanted to feel like the tsars of old. 

Everything they could find would go for it. They slaughtered cattle, looted more liquor stores and graved the most expensive cigars they could find. 

They were going to dine like kings and nothing was going to take this joy from their hands.
strings.YGR_regional.3.desc:
Ioseliani stumbled out of the hangar where another victory feast was being held, doubling over and vomiting, the alcohol running through his veins expelling itself. The night was dark and silent, aside from the shouts and light coming out of the hangar door. 

The Great Pakhan tensed up at hearing the crunch of footsteps behind him, his hand quickly finding his pistol and looking over his shoulder. 

“Ah... Rafael...” 

Ioseliani's face was stony as he straightened out and looked around, checking for people listening in, and silently pushed the door closed, nodding to his underling, allowing him to speak. 

Rafael's eyes darted around.  

“Jaba, we have Usoyan's accountant under our control” 

Ioseliani's face lit up as he slurred. “Well lovely stuff! Just a little more and that Kurdish snake will show its head!” 

“Jaba, the pakhans are making moves.” 

“Fuck, Raf, be specific, the feast's still go-” 

“Some are stealing weapons, some are deviating from patrolling routes, some are setting up bases where they aren't supposed to... and the single person it all goes back to is... Ûsoyan. I think this may be the beginning of something big...” 

Ioseliani looked off into the dark, the haze of alcohol quickly being replaced with cold determination. 

“Bo-?” 

“Raf, get my coat.” 

“Wh-” 

“We've been waiting for this opportunity, Raf! That damn Kurd is gonna get his due. ALL OF THEM ARE GOING TO GET THEIR DUE!” The Great Pakhan's stride lost any of the drunk slowness as he walked away from the hangar. “Raf-”
strings.YGR_regional.4.desc:
Ioseliani looked at the coin he twirled between his fingers, flicking it on the table, it spinning with a small ring, before slamming it down and repeating the same motion, over and over as his thoughts drifted for the first time in the many years he had been pakhan, even before it gained a 'Great' and got a capital letter. 

The truths of the gulag were simple: get the loyal in power, get the strong under you, make sure your suck ups keep their heads down. 

It was easy to be pakhan if you had the strength for it, but being the Great Pakhan? 

He had thought for a band of aimless men with fists for weapons, now he had to command an army. When before he just needed to feed himself and his goons for a day or two, the files on his desk talked of tonnes of flour and rice that would go to women and children in the cities. When before a mistake could at worst lead to a couple of kicked-in heads, now a nation balanced on a razor. 

The Great Pakhan slammed the coin down again and looked at the surface, the face of Nicholas the II staring back, a rare keepsake that one of his thieves found in the ground in Vorkuta. Ioseliani blinked, for a small fraction of a second the face that displayed the rotten Tzar morphing into his own, smiling victoriously. The Great Pakhan looked at the coin again and smirked. 

Glory did not wait for him to get comfortable, it ran ahead, and his thieves and he layed catch-up. Past the Vorkuta guards, past the communists and the omskovite fanatics, past his competition, Ioseliani continued to chase that spark. 

Glory did not wait for anybody. 

Ioseliani stood up, flipping the coin and stuffing it into his jacket pocket.
strings.YGR_regional.4.a: So he will continue giving chase.
strings.YGR_regional.5.desc:
Ioseliani unfurled the map of Europe onto his desk.  Good maps were hard to find these days -- this was one of the only few they could get him that wasn't 30 years out of date, and the rather unfortunate state of much of it lying under the Nazi jackboot made things pretty hard for Jaba.  The Thieves demanded money and power for his loyalty, but with the Swastika flying from Amsterdam to Moscow, there weren't exactly a lot of options he had left. 

Earlier, he had considered opening relations with the United States.  CIA agents had already involved themselves in training his troops, no doubt in exchange for hefty amounts of money and other...less legal things that only the Thieves in Law could provide.  One problem.  The Americans were an ocean away, and other than the frozen Kara and Laptev seas, the Thief Territory was landlocked. 

That left him with one option.  The neutral nations of Europe.  The German Sphere might have been out of his hands, but there was still money to be found on the continent.  Brittany was a state not unlike his own, and for the right price, they'll trade with anyone.  Pulling out a marker, he circled the country before moving south.  Switzerland was another good option.  Neutral and rich.  Iberia and Italy were perhaps even more lucrative.  With empires of their own and mutual hate for the Germans, a lucrative relationship could be made, both with their governments, and with the Italian and Iberian Mafias.  The Great Pakhan smiled.  There was hope for Europe yet.
strings.YGR_regional.6.desc:
Franco looked much more imposing in the propaganda photos, thought Ioseliani.  The old man standing in front of him, cane in hand, didn't seem like an imposing figure.  However, even though he didn't know a word of Spanish, he heard enough of the Caudillo's voice to know that he was not a man to be trifled with.  The Spanish, for such a laid-back people, sure loved their formalities.  He had been greeted with fine food, a Flamenco show, and a drill demonstration from the Iberian Army.  

When he at last sat down with the Caudillo to talk business, he was surprised that the two had a lot in common.  Both men had come to power in a time when their nation was gripped in weakness and civil war, a sentiment that resonated in Franco, that he was sure of from his firm handshake and that rare genuine smile he saw from the dictator.  The deal was simple.  Iberia would formally end its German-directed embargo on the free Russian territories and recognize the West Siberian Thief Territory as an independent state able to do business with Iberian corporations.  

Camera crews filmed and shutters flashed as the two dictators shook hands for all Iberia to see.  Two men that had risen from irrelevance to the very top.  Perhaps a lesser man would have come back with nothing, but Jaba knew a fellow self-made man when he saw one.  It was the cunning of this world, those that took risks and played hard, that would win.  And together, the Spanish Bull could make the Russian Bear roar again.
strings.YGR_regional.7.desc:
“I do not see how your... organization could even benefit us.” Giuseppe let out a puff of smoke and stretched lazily. Ioseliani could understand the lack of sense of urgency in the mafioso's movements. In the end, the Great Pakhan had been effectively defanged to enter Cosa Nostra territory, no weapons, no associates, just him. They even took away the Imperial coin he kept for good luck. 

“Well, Mister-” 

“Padre.” Giuseppe leaned forward, “You will call me... Padre.” 

The Great Pakhan's lips reflexively thinned out, but he really had no choice. If he wanted to speak to the leader of the Sicilian Mafia, Giuseppe Genco Russo, he had to do it as a weaker associate, rather than a greater power. 

“Padre Giuseppe, I believe my nation has MANY benefits for your business.” God, Ioseliani hated being sober, he never felt anxious, but the acute feeling that every word was being judged as a life-or-death matter did not leave him. 

“After all, behind me is a whole country. Huge markets, privileges with my security services, so much untouched land that you can hide your longer-term merchandise.” 

“And what do you want then?” Giuseppe interrupted, his expression unreadable. 

“Well,” Ioseliani grinned confidently, “Arms, support, eased trade and diplomacy with your group, as well as information on Italy-dearest's further interests and movements.” 

Giuseppe's expression did not change, instead, it stayed static as the mafiosi considered. “Fine, this does interest me.” Suddenly the Padre's tone warmed, “A drink to the new partnership?” 

The Great Pakhan chuckled, “Sure, always wanted to try Prosecco.”
strings.YGR_regional.8.desc:
Ioseliani felt out of place at this table, his neatly-pressed suit incomparable to the lavishness of the international tycoons, let alone their diamond-studded wives, all wearing the same painted-on smiles. 

One of the presenters fumbled a paper, beginning to announce the next orator for the evening, “Well, and to our newly accepted guest of honour! While the Swiss Alps may never compare to the Urals I would like to welcome Mister Jaba IO- IOSE- !?” 

The Great Pakhan gave a wry irritated smile as he stood up, champagne in his hand, the glass giving a whine under the pressure of his fingers. “Ladies and Gentlemen, I would like to give a short toast before this evening moves forward!” 

The whole room applauded politely, but the coldness behind their eyes could not betray that this was a test... 

“All of us here, we are self-built men. Men who were given no quarter, and took none ourselves. Some during the Great Depression,” Several of the silver-haired monocles nodded, “Some during the trying times of the Great Patriotic- I mean, the Second World War,” This time it was the turn of the men of Ioseliani's age to grumble in agreement. 

“And some even now, during the Reich's attempts to get a foothold on both of our doorsteps. Therefore we must celebrate this liberty, this great gift granted to us, to work and to be rewarded! Tonight, we take it easy, but we must also take it now!” Ioseliani raised his champagne glass, the tycoons raising theirs in unison.
strings.YGR_regional.9.desc:
If North Russia had frozen him with ice, Northern France pelted Vadim with sloshing rain and howling wind, but unlike Northern Russia, he had nought but a leather jacket to combat the elements, each of his limbs feeling like it was cast from numb marble. 

“Damn fucking...” He swore under his breath as the salt sprays hit Vadim in the face, another barge lazily pulling into the port of Saint Malo, the grey waves parting underneath it, several exhausted French sailors trudging into port under the torrential rain. Though, one seemed to stay back, sitting on one of the crates with a dreary expression. 

Vadim felt a sudden empathy, “Guard duty?” 

The French soldier lifted his head, “Hm?” 

Vadim pointed at the boxes of guns his boss left him on guard duty with and then at his rifle, “Guard duty?” 

The French's face lit up with understanding, “Ah, surentez?” 

“Yes yes, er... surandes...” Vadim nodded. 

The French chuckled, fishing around in his pocket and taking out a cigarette pack and offering it to the equally exhausted Russian. “Sigaretenn?” 

“Sure...” Vadim took the cigarette, lighting the Frenchman's and then his, before turning back towards the Yugran barge, observing the crates of guns with a bored expression. The French, turned back to his.
strings.YGR_regional.10.desc:
Ioseliani leaned back in the chair, eyeing the two agents sitting across him, as well as the huge mirror window on the wall. My, this certainly felt familiar. 

“So no press conferences and smiling at the camera?” The Great Pakhan pronounced dryly, picking between his teeth with a nail. 

Even through their shades, Ioseliani noted the glances the two agents threw at each other.  

“While the United States are open to negotiation in supporting your efforts, Mister Ioseliani-” 

“You cannot parade a 'criminal', hm?” Ioseliani interrupted. 

The agent opened his mouth, closed it, then opened it again. “Yes...” 

An unpleasant silence filled the room. Ioseliani chuckled. “Funny from a nation whose founding idea was tax evasion. But otherwise, what can you give me? Have you received the list I sent you?” 

Some of the tensions subsided as the other agent smiled. “We have looked through your demands and found none of them to be unreasonable. Actually, upon looking over your situation, we found that your resolve in allowing free markets and competition warrants additional support.” 

A slip of paper with lines upon lines of equipment was slipped across the table, The Great Pakhan catching it and giving it a glance... 

Ioseliani stood up, before smiling, “So, we are doing this 'on the hush'?” 

The agents also stood up,
strings.YGR_regional.11.desc:
Agent Konrad sighed as he observed the thief militia that was put under his responsibility to be trained. While the CIA had arranged to send arms, they also got the bright idea to send actual military personnel to train these... thieves. 

Not a single one responded to names, many had utterly ignored him until their... 'pakhan'... had barked something in Russian, all of them suddenly straightened out and became at least partially workable. 

But this? This took the cake. Yesterday they were ordered to pick up their equipment, some unbranded military kits and now... 

“WHY?” Konrad rubbed his forehead while the pakhan relayed his message. 

Some of the soldiers stood with extra guns, while some held their night vision goggles like blunt weapons, clearly having exchanged them for extra pieces of whatever they wanted. 

There was the large unit that was Krokhin, also known by 'Alligator', who had exchanged his kit parts for MREs, slowly stuffing another packet of shredded beef down his gob, chewing lazily as he looked off into the distance with barely any attention. 

Then there was the anaemic 'Vova', his gear lacking in grenades but in surplus of three coats on his shoulders, staring back with an innocent look in his eyes. 

Konrad's eyes stopped on 'Pero' Pechurin and asked him directly. 

“WHY, PECHURIN!?” 

The thief smiled from under the monopolized mountain of helmets, his golden teeth reflecting amiably.
strings.YGR_regional.12.desc:
Batov marched in front of the row of soldiers, observing the new form of armed forces he would command. 

Some stood straight, he could recognize the deportment of his own officers, or of the forces of Kaganovich, some like the Omskovites didn't even seem to breathe. There was the more relaxed ones, Dragunov's boys. The last ones were of course the bandits, none having uniforms, many exchanging jokes as Batov passed them. 

The general turned on his heels, observing the line of mix-and-matched soldiers. “Krotov through Kalmikin, re-do basic training.”  

The line of bandits went silent, shocked. “All the bandit forces are to re-do basic training, including discipline training and uniform rules.” The General looked at the rest and shouted, “Toooooo the right!” 

The line turned ninety degrees, even the shocked bandits following orders. 

“Foooorward... MARCH!” The soldiers marched away towards the barracks, leaving Ioseliani, who up to now sat lazily on the sidelines, observing the General, and Batov alone on the field. 

Ioseliani broke the silence. “What the fuck was that? I thought we were working together you dust-bag!” 

Batov was not at all shifted by the change in tone. “The Territory's forces are not ready for combat, they lack discipline and they cannot follow orders efficiently, that is the base of the army.” 

“Look, old boy,” Ioseliani sat forward, it was clear he was barely containing his anger. “Each gang has a right to express their way in combat, you don't-” 

Batov chuckled. “Well, if they keep trying to undermine overall order, it won't matter how unique they are if they're dead in a ditch. When the sun goes down-”
strings.YGR_regional.13.desc:
Pyotr scratched his beard with the dirt-covered rubber gloves, as always disappearing into his own thoughts as he tended to his field. 

But why the name, the Thieves? He could not really put a finger on it.  

Sure, their language was generally dirty, their attire was terrible and they carried guns wherever they went and used them with little to no control, but who didn't?  

Pyotr, in fact, saw LESS theft, not more than when Kaganovich was still the man with the crown. And working wasn't as unpleasant, after all, your own field feels much better than a community one, and who was he to start lying to himself? 

Yeah, they collected taxes, but at least they had the conscience to send some foul-mouthed gang pup to explain it first, rather than barging in and taking whatever they wanted.  

And the weekends? Pyotr had not had a weekend since... Well, he could not even remember when! Sure, he got longer breaks on Sundays, but otherwise, it was labour for 'The People' and 'The Party', day in and day out.  

And the sales! He'd never even bought or sold anything before! Sure, he bartered but knowing that you could trade for a day's food and some new book with the paper stacks you got from a tonne of potatoes somehow felt more reassuring than hoping that the Narkom was in good spirits on one day or another. 

Why, the fact he even thought about books was surprising! A couple of years back and he would just stare at those hieroglyph slips without a thought in the world! 

No, maybe they called themselves Thieves, Pyotr considered.
strings.YGR_regional.13.a: But he sure didn't see it..
strings.YGR_regional.14.desc:
Sergei Vorontzov pushed his cracked spectacles up his nose nervously, looking up at the entrance into what used to be... No, what is his land. The ten-hectare piece of land was good for a peasant farmer, in the better times... 

Sergei shook the apparition away with a shake of the head, before pushing the creaking gates open and walking in, the single bag on his back weighing on his weary shoulders covered in a dusty telogreika. 

His house was gone, so was his family, and while it was not something unexpected, he still felt a small painful pang in his heart. Instead, there was a single barn, a left-over of the collective that farmed the land. Wandering up to it, the old 'kulak' dropped his bag at the doorstep, turning around and sitting down on the dusty wooden stairs to observe his returned lands. 

Thirty years? Forty? His hand slowly found the small wooden cross on a rope and grasped it. Omsk, Sverdlovsk, Salechard, Vorkuta. They chased them further North then, farther from possible escape and warmer survivable weather. Farther from home. Farther from- 

The old man opened his mouth, clenching his teeth. “I'm home, Varvara... I'm home... I told you I would only be a while...”
strings.YGR_regional.14.a: A journey the length of a lifetime...
strings.YGR_regional.15.desc:
Ioseliani tapped the pen on the paper, lifting his eyes at the mayor of the town. 

“Is that all?” 

The young man nodded, scratching his cheek, a prison tattoo on the top of his hand showing a smoking skull. 

“Certainly is. The people need some education, not enough engineers for the electrical substation. Also, the food reserves could get a re-fill, what with the collective farms being an utter fucking bust-” 

The Great Pakhan sighed, “Yeah yeah, stop yapping, I'm thinking.” It certainly was a poignant problem, but the people were not only split by their identities, but by even how they got their daily piece of bread. 

Omskovites and Kaganovich's clique worked by what was essentially a command economy, Zlatoust stood on a sheer capitalist economy, though its social net was barely existent. Rokossovsky was a military junta and it worked completely by rationing, in the end, an army by itself was not very effective. 

But what was going to be THEIR economy? Ioseliani suddenly remembered the greatest mafiosis of his time. 

Al Capone, Siegel, Dillinger, all of them had tied the system around their finger, and which system was it? 

Ioseliani felt a grin spread on his lips. 

“I think we should privatize, I mean-”
strings.YGR_regional.16.desc:
Alexander stared at the two mooks sitting at his family table, his wife and children standing to the side, their looks teetering on mute terror.  

“Ah! The owner's here! Come on in!” The thinner bandit grinned and waved Alexander forward, to the table. While his exterior did seem friendly, the shopowner could not take his eyes off of the rifle on the bandit's knees. 

Alexander sat down and interlocked his fingers to control the shaking that entered his hands. “G-good evening. How may I help you?” 

“We have been hearing that your business is struggling, Mister Koroviev?” The taller bandit sat forward, observing the shopkeeper with a saccharine grin. 

“W-well...” Alexander was about to burst into hopeless tears, they were right, completely right. He did not have even enough money to get drivers for the goods trucks and had to drive them himself, but how could he tell that to the men who took gold and handed out lead at a moment's notice. 

The shopkeeper sighed, collecting all of his courage. Lying was pointless, and he wanted to make sure that whatever happens, he would not be remembered for cowardice. “Yes, I am struggling-” 

“Well, that's perfect! Congratulations, Mister Koroviev! Our local administration had heard these rumours and decided to help.” 

Alexander was stunned, “P-pardon?” 

“You shall be receiving pay-outs starting next month to keep your business running. Though there is a condition.” The taller bandit sat forward. 

Alexander nodded anxiously. “That being..?” 

The thin thief chuckled.
strings.YGR_regional.16.a: “We order you, you follow us! Simple as!”
strings.YGR_regional.17.t: Between a Rock And A Hard Place
strings.YGR_regional.17.desc:
The Great Pakhan put the cigarette out on the table, forcing an annoyed look from Batov. 

“Careful, these maps can go up in flames at a second's notice.” The General's hand carefully pushed the huge rolls to the side, farther from the black spot on the surface. 

Ioseliani snorted and took a few more gulps from his bottle, “Enough with the semantics! What do we have?” 

Batov sighed, unfurling the map, “Two fronts, the West, and the East. Up to now, neither has agreed to diplomatic dialogue, yet, at least.” 

“Mhm mhm.” The Great Pakhan grumbled, scratching his chin. 

“In the West, we have the most industry of the past union. Big cities, huge factories, more infrastructure. Though fighting them will probably hurt like a bitch, considering that it was one of the most fractured regions, and it faced Finland off, they probably have much more experience.” 

“And the East?” Ioseliani interrupted, his eyes thoughtful. 

Batov traced the Eastern frontier of their holdings. “Deeper into Siberia. Less infrastructure, but the whole region has benefited a great deal from the remains of Bukharin's so-called 'Siberian plan'. I do not know how much of it we can seize, but with the terrain and the lesser number of big cities can be challenging.” The General stopped, looking over the Great Pakhan. 

“So? Where should we focus the forces?” 

Ioseliani snapped out of his thoughts, before yawning. 

“So the West's got most of the industry... that means most of the financial remains are there as well?” 

Batov blinked. “I... suppose?” 

Ioseliani smiled knowingly, “Then what are we waiting for?”
strings.YGR_regional.18.desc:
Maria looked at her son entering the apartment, instantly noticing the scuffed uniform. 

“Vanechka, what happened, hm?”  

The young boy looked down at his shoes, before muttering, “A fight...” 

Maria shook her head and sighed, “Come, sit down.” The boy would drop his school bag, and sit down at the dinner table, still not looking up from his knees. 

The young woman would sit down across him, “You know you can't keep going like this, right? Vanechka?” The boy would not respond. “Every week you come back like this, all dirty and beat, you HAVE to start growing up, son. You cannot solve your problems with your fists-” 

“It's all Zhenka's fault!” The boy would shout, raising his eyes, clearly about to burst into angry tears. “We promised that we wouldn't give each other out! Just because I stole some chalk, he gave me out like a dirty rat!” 

Maria sighed, keeping her voice as even as possible, “Vania, that is still not-” 

“Then why's Dad allowed to, and I'm not! I heard vors are supposed to look out for each other!” 

The young woman barely contained the surprise, “W-well...” 

The boy would sob and run out of the room, knocking over the chair, slamming the door behind him. 

“Vania!” Maria would try to follow but then sat back down, sighing again and rubbing her forehead. 

She did not know why her husband, a supposed vor v zakone, one who was never supposed to work with the government, suddenly became the Chief of local Police, or how he permitted himself to marry even though vors supposedly never married. She could not wrap her head around it either, just as her son.  

“'Vors', 'promises', 'honour'...”
strings.YGR_regional.18.a: “God, they're no more mature than Vania...”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.1.desc:
Heinrich Himmler looked at the many forms on his desk.  Since Degrelle's disappearance, it had seemed that further threats to his Ordenstaat were falling one by one. Grabbing the next sheet of paper, he signed another execution order for some French traitor.  A shame, really. So many useful people kept getting themselves killed. It wasn't that hard to understand the supremacy of the Aryan, was it? Why would someone align themselves with such inferior beliefs? 

His thoughts were interrupted by the knock of a junior SS officer on the door.  

“Come in.” 

“Mein Reichsführer,” the young bureaucrat mumbled nervously, as he handed a thick folder, stamped “STRENG GEHEIM: NUR FÜR DIE AUGEN DES REICHSFÜHRERS”, to the most dangerous man in France.  “It seems that...” 

“Speed it up, boy, I'm not mad at you, no need to be so formal. Yet.” 

With the scolding clearly heard on his face, the officer handed Himmler the folder. Himmler walked back to his desk, unclasping the hinge and taking out what looked to be the largest report he had ever received. It dwarfed even the most verbose of Ribbentrop's dossiers, before the dolt got himself killed. 

As he read, however, it was clear why it was so long. 

The report detailed what was probably the most absurd, pathetic, and horrible thing that had ever happened within his domain. If what was written was true, the country had quite literally been robbed by Russian bandits. 

A young Yugran agent, who happened to know German well enough to pass off as Flemish, had climbed up the barbed, electrified, and heavily guarded border fence, snuck into the country, and had slowly infiltrated the Walloonian Legion. Eventually, the subhuman broke into a nuclear silo, put the highly radioactive warhead into a derelict suitcase, and hopped the border back into Germany. 

Why why why why why why why why WHY.  

Himmler began shaking. Very visibly. 

“You're telling me that some Russian criminal worm crossed the greatest border the world has ever seen, snuck into a nuclear missile silo, and managed to WALK out of here with one of our nukes? As if we were dimwitted Bolsheviks?”  

There was no reply. 

“I want the that silo's commander head removed off his fucking shoulders. Is that understood?” 

“Y-yes, my Reichsführer.” 

“Now get the fuck out of my office!”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.2.desc:
Jaba Ioseliani took a good look at his new dacha as he got out of the banya.  Ironically located in the idyllic woods outside of Omsk of all places, it was luxuriously decorated and a far cry from the usual pre-war cottages most had for summer homes.  He slid into the cold lake, the shock of the frigid ice water waking his whole body.  Life was good, he thought to himself.  After all, he was lucky to even be alive. 

The escape from the Vorkuta gulags was tough enough.  That bastard Blokhin acted like the Union had never fallen, working him and his fellow thieves to the bone.  He laughed a little thinking about the look on Vasily's face when it was the thieves throwing him into prison to rot.  

Oh, those early years were nothing but struggle.  Stalin, Rokossovsky, Yazov, Batov, the names flew through his head.  They were all stronger, their armies fierce remnants of the Old Union while he could only call upon a ragtag militia of thieves.  But the Thieves were stronger in the end. They always were because those generals and politicians could never understand that when the going gets tough, it's cunning that wins out. 

And now, the wolves were feasting.  His realm stretched from the border with German-occupied Russia to the expanse of Central Siberia to his east.  The Thieves were no longer a tired band of escaped prisoners, and Ioseliani wasn't just the Great Pakhan.  He was meant to be the leader of all Russia.  The realization shocked him more than the freezing waters.  As he pulled himself out of the lake and went back inside to dry off, he realized, now more than ever, that all of Russia was his for the taking.  He couldn't shy away from it now.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.3.desc:
Levon breathed heavily, his weight put against the wall, his back hunched over as he tried to keep his gastric juices down, gagging at the sight in front of him. “W-WHAT THE FUCK!?”  

Patunin, on the other hand, looked at the body with a cold disconnection. “Well, Leva, get the bag from the motorcycle.” The ex-militsioner observed the scene, noting the boot sizes and the position of the beaten and broken cadaver in front of them. The remains of the ex-komissar in front of them had been kicked and stoned to death by some gang or other, and Patunin supposed that the only reason HE wasn't in that place himself was how unforgivingly corrupt he has been his whole life.  

The younger man tried to straighten out and walk, before groaning and nearly dropping to his knees, his breakfast almost spilling onto the asphalt.  

The ex-policeman sighed, walking up to Levan, patting his back, “Come on, Leva! They handed you over from the Army, you gotta have seen at least a FEW bodies-” 

“Goh... Papanya, you don't see this kinda stuff in the army- HURP-” As the younger man's words were cut off, Patunin jumped back to avoid getting his shoes painted by vomit and swore under his breath. 

First, he was a gumshoe, but after he hit his prime, the promotion finally came and the cushy job rolled in with it, until they figured out where all those finances went that is. Several years in the gulag, and now he was back to THIS... Only that he was serving with the same men he shared a cell with not so long ago. 

“Fucking hell...” Pulling Levon up by the elbow, he would drag him out to the motorcycle, propping his 'protege' up against the sidecar and taking the 'police'-issued potato sack to put the corpse in. 

“Catch your breath, Alisa said they found more like this, so we have a long day ahead.”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.4.desc:
“The what now?” Lukov lifted an eyebrow questioningly at his son and took a sip of his Sunday morning coffee. In the end, the fried exotic beans were still an expensive commodity, so treating himself once a week was the most he could do. 

“Providence/stay! They show it on TV after the news!” Oleg was quite smart for a twelve-year-old, the pair of glasses Lukov smuggled in for the adopted orphan causing the boy's grades to 'suddenly' jump, but considering how he hoped his adopted son would grow up, the rugged bandit was a little disappointed. “It's gonna start in ten minutes! Let's watch!” 

“Alyosha... Are you not a bit too old for cartoons?” While Lukov tried to phrase the absent-mindedly spoken phrase without any offence, the boy's enthusiasm would suddenly extinguish.  

“O-oh, s-sorry, right...” The boy would lower his head a little. 

Lukov sighed, “Well, considering how well you've been in school, maybe I was a little harsh.” The bandit placed down his mug. “Let's go watch together for a bit, hm?” 

Oleg would perk up, “Right! You're gonna love it!” He would grab the man's hand, pulling him towards the living room of their shabby apartment, “It's got this school guy who fights against historical figures and, like, they gotta fight until only one is left to reclaim-”  

Lukov rolled his eyes a little, quickly getting lost in his son's incomprehensible explanation of the plot, but coming along anyways and sitting in front of the TV. 

With a click, the screen lit up. 

“It's already started!” 

Lukov did not really get why the proportions of the characters were so bizarre, big eyes, colourful hair but aside from the crude shapes, one thought occupied the back of his mind...
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.4.a: “Christ, what are the kids even watching these days...”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.4.b: “Not too bad, maybe Oleg's onto something...”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.5.desc:
“Jaba!” Ivan burst through the door, the letter of forced resignation still in his hand. “Jaba! You bastard! You cannot do this to m-” 

Ioseliani would open his eyes, yawning lazily and standing from his armchair, stretching slightly. 

“Are you listening to me!? This is bullshit! THIS IS FUCKING BULLSHIT! I SERVED YOU WELL AND GOOD! I-” 

 POW! 

Ivan fell back, his jaw giving way to the Great Pakhan's knuckles with a sickening crack, the ex-officer giving a pitiful howl and holding onto his face as his ears rang. 

“You enter into my office,” Ioseliani kicked him in the ribs, “Wake me the fuck up,” Another kick, another terrified grunt, “And tell me I CANNOT DO SOMETHING THAT'S WRITTEN IN THE THIEF'S LAW, YOU LITTLE RUNT!” The last kick would cause Ivan to roll over on his back now holding on to both his face, blood running from his mouth and nose, the punch having made good contact. 

Jaba would lean forward, “By the Thief Laws, your actions at Vorkuta in aiding the Usoyani forces are to be considered TREACHERY, and it doesn't matter if it was BEFORE sides were chosen, so, you little fucking mongrel, don't you fucking DARE disturb my nap with your yapping when you are a clear cut traitor...” 

Ioseliani grinned, “By law, you are a nobody, got it? Not a Thief anymore... But I also did it because I fucking hate you, Ivan, and I always hated you.” 

Ivan would try to scramble back only to receive a kick to the face, blood droplets hitting the floor.  

“Who gave you the right to even CONSIDER a place as a general? You were always uppity.” Ioseliani spit on the floor, turning around and walking back to his armchair. 

“Alright, now get the fuck out of my sight before I blow your brains out, filthy traitor.” The last part was said with a pleased demonstrative close of the eyes.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.5.a: Laws are written to be abused.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.6.desc:
Artur Cohen sighed and rubbed his hands, trying to ease his nervousness. He never had the chance to return to teaching after the war had failed. No, he barely had time to save himself, to run further East, hiding his Jewish roots. 

“She just ran into my fist!” The girls in front of his desk were both students, both of them on the way to graduation. While he could not remember the name of the first one off the top of his head, the little mutt that stood to the right of her, her name he knew VERY well. Sofia Berezovskaya. 

The daughter of the local Pakhan snickered self-indulgently. “I said, SHE RAN INTO MY FIST, YOU OLD OWL!”  

Cohen considered standing up and grabbing the little bitch by the ear. 'Ran into her fist', what utter bollocks, this generation knew nothing about discipline, let alone simple empathy. 'Old owl', if he was still in the Union, she would be on cleaning duty for the next decade for insulting a teacher! 

Then his mind jumped to her father. If the principal disciplined her, what was next? Berezovskiy did not need to send an army to Cohen's door. It was simple. His papers would start 'getting lost' in the bureaucracy, the school's investors would all suddenly pull out for various reasons, local businesses would serve him badly or not serve him at all. 

“Is that true, Masha?”  

The girl with the black eye would sniffle and nod. Cohen ground his teeth but opened his mouth. 

“Then there is no more problem, return to classes.” 

As the two left, Sofia would shove Masha through the door, giggling. Cohen sat back in his chair and rubbed his face. No, he would never have had the chance to rebuild a school before the Thieves came in.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.7.desc:
Ioseliani felt a sense of deja vu, as he walked into the room of generals, all of them around the map of Russia as Batov continued explaining something in a focused manner, the only light being the huge lamp in the centre of the room as it shone on every crease of the paper. 

“Planning the march East, eh?” The Great Pakhan took a swig from his bottle, walking up to the table, the generals parting to let him through, leaving only Batov standing on the opposite side of the table. 

“We certainly are.” Batov responded absent-mindedly, tracing his finger on the Eastern front. 

“So, old boy, what do you have for me?” Ioseliani kicked a chair to the table, sitting down and taking on his usual bored expression. 

Batov lifted his eyes. “Well, for starters we have some good understanding of the enemy's industry centres.” He traced his finger on the southern border. “The Northern climate makes it hard for any city to develop well, so going too far North, or committing more forces there will probably result in resource starvation and useless land.” 

“So what do you propose?” Ioseliani had by now gotten used to Batov's self-centred style of explanation. The General knew what he was doing when it came to strategy and tended to get wrapped up in his own thoughts, the Great Pakhan just had to listen. 

Batov smiled, his eyes still on the map. “Either we use overwhelming forces to crush the clearly less-protected north and encircle the heavily armed south, or we utilize Omsk as a shield to exhaust them.” 

Ioseliani grinned, getting up. “It seems you have it under control.” While the phrase seemed to be directed at the whole group of generals, Batov could swear he had seen a respectful nod towards himself as the Great Pakhan departed.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.7.a: Never disturb a great craftsman in his labour.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.8.desc:
Otto nervously scratched the back of his head, the aged administrator rubbing his hands as the two men in the worn SS uniforms observed the warhead that was snuck out through the service tunnels, the greyed man in a lab coat that came with them checking some parts and pieces, the Geiger counter in his hand picking up small disturbances. 

“I-is everything up to expectation?” The two men turned their heads at Otto's inquiry, one of them chuckling, while the third one continued checking the warhead. 

The nearest man in the SS uniform, the blonde, as if he came straight off of a propaganda poster, turned back to the lab-coated individual pronouncing something in Russian, Otto grimacing at the Untermensch language. 

The 'professor' lifted his head, turning off the Geiger counter and nodding. 

The blonde turned back to the administrator, sighing and unbuttoning the black jacket, Otto feeling a freezing block of ice drop into his stomach. Was he a loose end to them..? 

“P-please I have a wife, sh-she's sick, I swear it's the real thi-” The blonde came up to Otto at a leisurely pace, reaching for something in the inside jacket pocket, “P-please...” 

A stack of papers was stuffed into his hands, the administrator pausing, terror changing to surprise. 

“Shut the fuck up. Two passports to Switzerland, two 'mill' dollars on the offshore account,” The blonde pronounced with a deep Russian accent, grinning. “Now fuck off, Papasha, deal is done.” 

Otto wiped away the drop of cold sweat as the three turned to the nuclear-laden truck, boarding it to depart back to whatever Untermensch hellhole they were from, several joking in-between each other and laughing as they went.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.8.a: Not even the Aryan man can withstand the call of Capital.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.9.desc:
Stepan had Volga German roots, however, in the end, the only thing that mattered was that he could speak German and had blonde hair. You wouldn't be able to get a more 'Aryan' Slav if you combed through the whole of Europe. And the Yugran bandits could not believe their luck when that 'Aryan' was found in a local bandit. 

On the other hand, Arkadiy did not look Aryan. The smuggler's black hair, brown shifty eyes, and small stature looked nothing like the posters, but in the end, Ost-Paris met the two as warmly as a breezeblock regardless. 

It was early morning, the two have already awakened in the abandoned bunker hidden within the forest floor and pulled on their smuggled SS uniforms, trying their best to not let the anxiety get to them. 

“Stepka, I'm gonna go check what's up-top, you go get the docs, got it?” Stepan nodded, turning to Arkadiy's backpack, the latter would slowly push the rusted trapdoor of the bunker open, peering through the small gap, seeing if any patrol was passing through. 

Silence... 

“I think it's-” Arkadiy would go quiet, as he heard the hurried shuffle of fallen leaves on the ground, but continued observing. 

The Frenchman must have escaped the daily march to the work camp, but the state he was in, it was surprising he could even run, his skin hanging off of him like ill-fit clothing, his eyes sunken into the skull. “Non! Non! S'il vous plait, n-” Arkadiy heard a click somewhere in the distance and- 

“There they are,” Stepan finally found the documents turning back to his comrade, only to find the man sitting against the closed bunker trap door, his face ashen. 

“Arka, 'sup with you?” 

“I think...” He mumbled.
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.9.a: “I think we should wait for a bit...”
strings.YGR_FEMBOY_IOSELIANI_YES: You watch the TV with him in curiosity...
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.10.desc:
“So what's the show even about?” Vlad still felt, to say the least, sceptical about Kydyr's invitation to watch a cartoon, of all things. 

In return, his bandit friend would sigh and knock some ash off of his cigarette. “Providence lore? I'm pretty sure the fuckers up in the state departments specifically made it impenetrable so that some jackboot fuck can't make sense of it.” 

This did not fill Vlad with confidence as he continued to stare blindly into the screen, “Isn't there... a shortened version?” 

Kydyr paused, staring into the box of the smuggled TV, clearly trying to formulate his idea as some weirdly shaped character pummelled another weirdly shaped character. “Well... Okay, imagine every other century a lotta very rich mad fucks get together to fight to the death.” 

“Right, so basically pakhans.” 

“Yeah, sure, pakhans. A couple of pakhans gather up every other century and fight to the death so that the survivor can get a chance to get a wish granted to them by the Golden Fleece.” 

“Aaaand, that's it..?” 

“They also summon some historical figures as their 'companions' in fights. Lotsa magical bullshit. Just roll with it...”  

Vlad was feeling unsure if he wanted to really watch it anymore... 

“So... they summon anyone?” 

“Hm? Oh yeah, Giordano Bruno, Carl Friedrich Wagner, Nevsky, Pushkin, Peter the Great...” 

“Anyone more modern?” 

“Yeah, kinda why I invited you, they're gonna reveal the Great Pakhan's companion form.” 

“Companion? Wouldn't they want him to be one of the guys fighting?” 

“It's Providence lore, don't worry about it- Wait there it is!” Kydyr sat forward, “They're summoning him!” 

Vlad also sat forward, “Get outta the way you're blocking the screen!” 

“Oh shush! Lemme-” Kydyr paused, his expression turning to shock... “Gaha... GAHAHAHA!” The bandit fell back, his sides going into orbit from what he just saw. 

Vlad looked at the screen, seeing... a purple-haired... girl..? “W-why's the Great Pakhan a girl..?” He could barely contain the confused disgust in his tone. 

Kydyr sat up wiping his cheeks from the tears of laughter. “Gohoho... Oh man, Vladik, the funniest part-”
strings.YGR_superregional_ioseliani.11.desc:
Rafael carefully stepped into Ioseliani's office, a reflexive nervous gulp travelling down his throat. The room was a complete mess, papers lying around, some of them torn, some of them wet with what looked like whiskey stains, as if a booze-filled whirlwind burst through the room. 

“RAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAF!” The right-hand man finally noticed the Great Pakhan emptying one of the bookcases, looking for something, his usually slicked back hair in tufts, the smell of heavy booze in the air, “GET THE FUCK HERE, YOU SON OF A BITCH!” 

“H-hey, Boss...”  

Ioseliani looked up from the drawer, his eyes bloodshot, Rafael never having seen such an enraged expression on the man before. Standing up, Ioseliani would turn back to emptying the drawers, his jaw clenched. 

“Raf, who in fuck's name had let the Japanese into the propaganda department!?” 

“W-what?” 

The bookshelf would tumble to the floor with a great smash as the Great Pakhan pulled it down, looking around like a trapped beast and continuing his ruffle through the paperwork. 

“I said, WHO LET THE ASIANS INTO THE MOTHERFUCKING PROPAGANDA DEPARTMENT!?” 

Rafael blinked, trying to process. “Is there... a problem..?”  

“Yes! THAT!” Ioseliani pointed at his desk. Rafael would carefully tip-toe around the spilt papers and reach the desk. The only thing left on it was a small figurine of a... bandit? Bandit girl? The proportions were weird, eyes were slightly too big, the limbs a bit too thin, and the hair was... purple? She also seemed to look like a... teen? 

“What am I looking at, Boss?”  

“Their product! Told me they were gonna make a show, something about a good FUCKING IMAGE! GOOD IMAGE, MY BA-” Ioseliani pulled out the paper, slurring out a victorious 'Ah-ha!'. 

“OUT OF THE WAY, RAF! AND IF I SEE YOU TAKE THAT FIGURINE, YOU WILL REGRET IT FOR THE REST OF YOUR SHORT LIFE! NONE ON THIS LIST WILL LIVE TO SEE TOMORROW!” Ioseliani would burst out of the room, taking out his revolver as he went, the thing almost misfiring into his leg, leaving the right-hand man in shocked silence.
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.1.desc:
Usoyan sat at his desk, his fingers interlocked, the freezing night howling powerlessly against the glass of his window, the oil lamp casting a warm glow across his office. In such moments, he would cast his mind to the past, the Old World's siren call pulling him back 

Tbilisi, 24 years old, young and inexperienced, the next thing he knew one of the pigs had grabbed him and beat him into submission. Stealing didn't give him much, and the short death row did not reform him, but it sure as Hell taught him a lot about life. 

Aslan allowed himself a thoughtful scowl as he stared into the flickering flames. The Tiflis Three were strange beasts in his eyes. On one hand, their deaths got his jailers' heads torn off, on the other hand, while he may have escaped, his homeland lay under the same monster that ruined it since he was a child.  

When the jail guards got called off to fight, it did not take long to overpower the green boys they put up instead, and then he ran... Oh he ran, he sure did. Trekking across the Caucasus, further North, past the constantly changing warlord borders, with fake names and faker currency, meeting many, remembering few. 

Usoyan shook off the nostalgia, but as his hand reached to extinguish the flame of the lamp, muttered,“Tbiliso, mzis da vardebis mkhareo...”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.1.a: “Tbilisi, the side of sun and roses...”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.2.desc:
“The fuck do you mean we gotta answer for every bullet!?” Valygin almost spat with rage as he slammed his rifle on the desk. 

Xatun put down the smuggled porno mag, his expression showing that he would rather be anywhere but here, explaining to some mook why the arsenal started to keep tabs. 

“Valygin, tell me, do you get paid?” 

“Well, yeah, since last month.” 

“Right, so no more random looting raids. That also means that instead of letting you blockheads take any weapons and ammunition you like, we gotta collect it, mark it, sell it off...” 

“Right...” Valygin made a thinking face, Xatun continuing the logical chain. 

“So that we can buy ammo for YOUR guns, because you work for the Territory, right? And if we buy you ammo, instead of you taking it, whose ammo is it?” 

Valygin clenched his jaw.  

Xatun noticed the spark of understanding, “That's right, it's not YOUR ammo, it's OUR ammo, and if you're using OUR ammo, you're BORROWING it, you blockhead! Every time you chamber a round, that's territory budget getting fired through those skulls. And what do we do with money if we're not using it?” 

The bandit soldier sighed dejectedly, “We count it.” 

“Good job, Valygin, maybe you're not completely mentally deficient! Now get out and stop bothering me,”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.2.a: “Last time I heard, they'll be counting rifles soon.”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.3.desc:
“You look older, Diyar.” Aslan noted, looking at his men unloading the trucks of equipment in the distance, the smog of the early morning factories starting up making the machines look like giant bugs. 

“And your Kurdi is rusty, brother. None of us are getting younger.” Diyar took out a pack of cigarettes, putting one between his lips, Usoyan grimacing and looking away. 

“I simply wanted to offer you an exit, if you need it. I got myself land in the Russian Wastes, you can walk out of this and-” 

“And leave the sunny lands of the 'Black State' behind?” The grey-haired man lit his cigarette chuckling as he puffed on it. 

Usoyan's scowl only grew, “This cause, our cause, it's-” 

“Save your breath, brother, you'll just breathe more smog. You can tell me about how terrible Kaukasien is as much as you want, it won't matter considering I live it.” Diyar would stand up, wiping his hands on the camouflage pants. 

“Georgia wasn't all great, being that to them we were not their own. But in the end, this fight, it's not just for us, brother.” The old man pulled the strap of the machine gun over his shoulder, taking a few more puffs of his cigarette. 

“This isn't about being Kurdish, or Georgian, or hating the Germans. Men had stood and died to set us free again, the Tiflis Three let not one single scream when they hoisted them up. So,” Diyar turned back to Usoyan. “How am I to run away when the fight is just warming up, with your guns and all?” 

“I... I do not know.” Usoyan swapped his speech from Kurdi to Georgian, the older man, in turn, looking away before giving him a slap on the shoulder and grinning.  

“The fight is not over, Aslan. Not with you on our side. We will be free, brother. Just you watch us. Now go,”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.3.a: “Your path in Russia awaits you, just as mine awaits me here.”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.4.desc:
As the piggish mining executives argued over which parts of Russia they would rip open when the reunification is complete, Aslan realized that he truly, supremely did not care for these people. The Germans and the Japanese were more likely to use slave labor than hire Russians, and the Americans would probably underpay them. His thoughts were interrupted, however, by the first demands of the meeting; those of the large Reichswerke HG man. 

“Alright, Mr. Usoyan, we've looked over the geological data here, and...”began the man, before trailing off. His Russian was subpar. “...and we would like to mine here,” he pointed out on their map as he spoke, “here, and here.” He pointed to three hillside areas near the Moskowein-Russian border. With a disillusioned, if still loyal and dogmatic voice, he continued, “The Reich requests that you generously give us the mining rights for those three sites. The oil and other resources there are requested by the Reichstag itself,” 

“It will be considered, my friend,” Usoyan replied, as cordially as he could, for such a man, “However, I would still like to hear from the others before I make any final decision. Mr. Davenport, from Freeport McMoRan?” With his words, the American, a lean man obviously high on cocaine, stood, and pointed to a spot on the Kamchatka peninsula. 

“It says here that diamond and borax deposits center at this point, where my finger is? We wanna mine right there, yeah. You'll let us?” 

“Again, my friend, we must hear the requests of all parties,” Usoyan replied, with more control than with the German, “Mr. Aso, you actually run the mining company you represent, what do you wish to mine?” Takakishi Aso, head of the Aso mining company, rather than pointing on the map, began his request; 

“There's a hill near the Manchurian border, one with a yellowish scar on its side. We wish to run our mine on that hill, which is located...” He pointed to a hill on the map, some 290 kilometers away from the border, “...right there.” 

Usoyan stood for a moment, giving the appearance of deep thought. However, the mining operations were far from his thoughts; of course these people could mine there, even the Germans! They had no clue how much money they were going to make him. He finally answered; 

“Gentlemen, you have the permission of our organization to mine where you have each requested. The Reich, the Sphere, and the free world will have their mines.” With those words, Usoyan walked out, and several underlings rushed to each of the executives, giving them dozens of forms and paperwork to sign. 

For the first time in a while, Usoyan smiled.
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.5.desc:
“Prost!” Abs lifted the champagne glass, gnawing on his usual cigar, his little eyes darting from one company man to another, a knowing grin trudging up to his lips. 

“Prest!” Flick slurred, the corporation leader certainly had too many whiskies, his usual fiery temper now flickering in all directions like a flame in a strong wind, the glass between his fingers in a very unsure position. 

“Prost.” Geilenberg looked the most modest of them all, the glass of German beer being quite symbolic for the state-corporation puppet. 

“Certainly!” Siemens even stood up a little, his glass of wine held with a steady hand, but his cheeks slightly red, the old man also having relaxed with the coming of alcohol. 

“And to the destruction of those fu-!” Flick opened his mouth, about to go on another rant. 

“Yes yes, Friedrich, 'the lesser races', but let the guest of honour speak first.” Abs interrupted, stopping the situation from devolving further, curiously waiting for the last corporation leader to raise a toast. 

Usoyan grimaced as he looked at his new business partners, and picked up his glass of water, uninterested in alcohol. 

“Well, gentlemen, I suppose, prost.” 

Abs was almost glimmering, “To future success!”
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.6.desc:
Air was filled with cigar smoke. Radio played old, slow music while Usoyan sat in his office, looking outside the window. He spectated the scene outside, soldiers marching towards their duties, while on street people walked around, going to their jobs or going home. He had a big proud smile on his face. He ruled them all, high above the others in a way he only dreamed of as a boy.

 His calm was broken as someone knocked at the door. “Come in!” Usoyan shouted as he turned around to face the doors. It was Devdari, his right hand man.  “Everything is ready Sir. We are waiting for you to arrive.”

“Ah Devdari, my good old Devdari...” He said while lighting up another cigar.“You see all this? Do you see what we hold in our hand? This power that...some leaders would be able just to dream about?” He got up from a chair.“After all these years of fighting... it is time for a big move, for a big centralization. It is time to rebrand our company.” As he finished his little speech, he proceeded to the meeting that Devdari informed him about.
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.6.a: A toast to our future investments
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.7.desc:
Usoyan, dressed in all formals with a proud smile, headed towards the conference room. As he entered the room, all politicians and generals sitting at the table stood up, greeting him with respect. He sat at the head of the table. Silence spread through the room, with only the sound of papers moving being heard.

“Gentlemen!” he said, clearing his throat,“I think it's finally a time for us to speak about our opponents in Siberia. Our mighty state grew stronger over the recent period of time, and we can - we should - start preparing for the war that I see as the biggest one yet! But, we must not underestimate our opponents, who used these years to build up their own military and industry, thus posing a big threat to us. But let us not be discouraged by that sight - we will crush not only our most immediate adversaries, but every other madman that would dare to stand in our way towards the final and utmost conquest of all Russian lands!”

A small comotion appeared as he made a pause in his speech. Some people didn't accept it well, while others looked at him with a more or less well-hidden smile. Whispers filled the room, slightly breaking the silence. Then Usoyan continued talking.

“Gentlemen, I hereby advise that we immediately start preparing ourselves for the upcoming storm. We need our factories pumping out more guns, our men tough as steel, our generals ready to lead these same men into the battle! This said, the meeting is over. The fate of this country rests upon your shoulders, so don't screw this up.” After a brief moment of silence, Usoyan stood up and left the room with a quick step. The rest of the men present remained there for another couple of minutes, discussing what they just heard.
strings.YGR_superregional_usoyan.7.a: “This is going to be tough, my friend!”
strings.YGR_flavour.1.desc:
Sashka screamed as his comrade's head exploded from the sniper fire, falling backwards, feeling the burn of stomach acid rise up to the back of his throat as he felt the taste of copper in his mouth, blinded by the crimson on his face. 

“Vadim! God! VADIM!” His panicked shout was cut short with another shot, the spark of his mind going out permanently as half of his skull came off with the speed of the flying round, slumping onto the snow and staining it with red. 

The spotter, Catherine, would get out of cover first, followed by Arseniy, the two walking in utter silence, approaching the dead men. 

“Check his pockets first. Looks like an officer.” The bandit girl followed the sniper's orders and would lean down, beginning to riffle through what was Vadim's pockets. 

“Anything? Don't like being so far in the open.” 

“No, just usual communist threads and crumbs. Some ciggies though...” Catherine would take out an intricate metal cigar case, refurbished for holding shitty papirosa cigarettes, and flip it open, noticing the picture of what looked like a cossack and his wife. 

Her eyes would suddenly stop, admiring it. The refined deportment of the cavalryman, the dress of the woman. 

“Fuck are you waiting for? Can we sell anything, or fucking not?” Arseniy kept his rifle aimed at the woods, turning in circles, waiting for any possible looters to come and take their 'prey'. 

“Yeah... probably.” Catherine would take the photo out, crumple it, and stick it into the bullet hole in the officer's head, cackling as she stuffed the cigarette case into her pocket. 

“Let's go. Nothing left of these losers, and soon the wolves will start swarming for them.” The two would begin walking away, as the two bodies began to freeze in the snow.
strings.YGR_flavour.1.a: In a world of insanity, nothing is sacred.
strings.YGR_flavour.2.desc:
Usoyan wrinkled his nose at the smell of cigar smoke and alcohol as he opened the door into the darkened depths of the Great Pakhan's office. 

Ioseliani was asleep again, his dirty boots propped up on the desk as he lay back in his leather armchair, the cap pushed down over his eyes. The Kurd's jaw clenched as he walked up to the desk, and cleared his throat. 

“Pakahn Ioseliani.” 

Ioseliani would grumble something similar to a swear under his breath and slowly push the visor above his eyes with his index finger. 

“Hm? Ah... Usoyen?” 

“Usoyan.” 

The Great Pakhan smirked, finding his purposeful mispronunciation somehow humorous, Usoyan's lips thinned out as he placed the paper list in front of Ioseliani. 

“Here's a list of the newly ascended pakhans in the last month, to share.” 

Ioseliani yawned, grabbing the list lazily, his eyes beginning to scan the names, and absent-mindedly pronouncing, “Bit of whiskey?” 

“I do not drink on workdays.” The Kurd responded curtly. 

“Then take a seat-” 

“I have no time to LAZE around AIMLESSLY.” 

Now this DID cause Ioseliani to raise his eyes from the list, measuring Usoyan up predatorily, before snorting and tossing the list onto the desk in front of him. 

“Well, if you did your job better, Usoyen, maybe you WOULD have the time. You're missing Popov and Kikvadze, next time double-check your shit before waking me up.” 

The Great Pakhan would lean back into the leather chair yet again, and nonchalantly push the cap back over his eyes, signalling the conversation was over and that Usoyan should take his leave. 

Barely containing his frustration, with teeth grinding, Usoyan left the office. In that moment, both of them shared only one thing in common. One thought. One phrase.
strings.YGR_flavour.3.desc:
“Check-mate.” Usoyan placed the weathered piece forward, Ilo's eyes bulging as he silently mouthed to himself, taking in the whole board, before finally seeing how his King was locked into place and put down, sighing and scratching the back of his head. 

“Good game, sir.” The right-hand man would stand up and straighten the creases on his grey jacket and corrected his worn tie. 

“Certainly.” The Kurd swiped the pieces into the chess box and shut it, putting it away emotionlessly. 

Usoyan did not like the ruffle and dirt of the average bandits, those more reminding him of some mentally deficient green army peasants he heard so many stories of in his childhood. But Ilo Devdari signified the complete opposite, the man almost always well-groomed, eloquent and most importantly, still retaining his deadliness. 

“Anyways, while it was a good break from my duty, sir, I need to get onto the task you gave me.” Ilo would take out a cigarette, but noticing Usoyan's grimace would silently place it back in his pocket, not requiring a worded complaint. 

And yet, for all of the man's similarities to a Cosa Nostra grunt, or a corporate dog that Usoyan wanted to emulate in his men, there was still that unbreakable lingering smell of shit, un-business-like activities, self-indulgence... 

“Of course, Rafael Baghdasaryan... Keep track of him, if you may. The man may seem weak-willed, but considering that he works under that oaf, he probably has several surprises that I would prefer to be neutered when the time comes.” 

Ilo took out his butterfly knife, the 'feather' whistling as he flipped it open, “And if he is open for a 'present', so to say?” 

The Kurd smiled.
strings.YGR_flavour.4.desc:
“What did you say about my mother, you fucking katzap!?” Ayaz hissed, standing up from his kneeling position next to the bottle of cheap-shit beer he and his mates had decided to share. 

“I called her a whore, a fucking whore, kozyol!” Vanya 'Scissors' gave his brand smile, his hand travelling to his pocket, his weapon of choice in the form of sheep sheers resting comfortably in his hand. 

“Van'ka, I don't think it's worth it...” Dmitry on the other hand did not keep anything in his pockets, but as a right-hand man of the small gang of delinquents, he had to be present for what essentially came down to a dick-measuring contest. 

“Shut it! It's just getting interesting!” Scissors hissed through his teeth, turning back to Ayaz. “So, you fucking sheep-fucker, what are you gonna do about it!? Or what,” Vanya nodded to the side, turning the opposing gang's attention to the rest of the dozen-or-so other young men, several armed with rusty pipes or broken bottles. “, Don't got the guts?” 

“You really,” Ayaz, infamous for his rage, bit his tongue, barely containing himself, “REALLY don't want this!” The roar alarmed the rest of his gang, several also standing up, picking up bricks and bottles. 

“Van'ka... stop...” Dmitry reflexively took a stance, his hand finding the gas pistol in the inside of his pocket. 

“You keep shitting yourself, you'll be sitting in it for the rest of your life!” Scissors grinned, “Let's fucking go!” And burst forward.
